# [부호화/특수점수] INCOM2

## 별칭/검색어

- INCOM2
- incongruous combination level 2
- 부당결합 수준 2
- 모순적 결합 수준 2

## 핵심 정의

`INCOM2`는 하나의 대상 안에 묶인 요소들의 결합이 매우 부적절하고 분명히 기괴해서, 수준 2로 평가되는 부당결합 특수점수다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 서로 어울릴 수 없는 부위나 속성이 한 대상 안에서 매우 기괴하게 결합되면 `INCOM2`를 준다.
- 반응 전체가 수준 1보다 훨씬 더 부자연스럽고 뚜렷하게 이상하게 들리면 `INCOM2`를 검토한다.
- 색과 형태의 조합이 현저하게 부적절하고 기괴하면 `INCOM2` 가능성을 본다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- 수준 2인지 확신이 없으면 `INCOM2`가 아니라 `INCOM1`을 준다.
- `INCOM2`도 여전히 `하나의 대상` 내부 결합 문제다. 둘 이상의 대상 사이 관계 이상은 `FABCOM2`와 구분해야 한다.
- 단일 영역 안에서 두 인상이 오염적으로 합쳐지면 `CONTAM`과 구분해야 한다.
- `INCOM2`는 Level 2 special score이므로 이후 `Lv2`, `WSum6` 문맥과 연결되지만, coding 단계에서는 먼저 반응의 기괴성을 본다.

ko.title: [부호화/특수점수] MOR
ko.bodyMarkdown:
# [부호화/특수점수] MOR

## 별칭/검색어

- MOR
- morbid content
- 손상반응
- 병적 내용

## 핵심 정의

`MOR`는 대상이 죽었거나, 파괴되었거나, 손상되었거나, 망가진 상태로 확인되거나, 우울하고 침울한 성질이 대상에 직접 부여될 때 붙이는 특수점수다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 대상이 죽은 것, 부서진 것, 찢어진 것, 불탄 것, 썩은 것, 상처 입은 것, 망가진 것으로 분명하게 확인되면 `MOR`를 준다.
- 사람, 동물, 식물, 사물처럼 내용 종류와 상관없이 손상 또는 파괴 상태가 반응의 핵심이면 `MOR`를 검토한다.
- "슬픈 나무", "침울한 집"처럼 우울하거나 황폐한 성질이 대상에 직접 붙으면 `MOR`를 준다.
- `MOR`는 위치, 결정인, 내용 코드를 대신하지 않고 추가로 붙는 특수점수다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- 무섭다, 불쾌하다, 이상하다는 느낌만으로는 `MOR`가 아니다. 대상의 손상성이나 병적 성질이 명시되어야 한다.
- 공격 행동이 일어나는 장면은 `AG`를 먼저 검토하고, 그 결과 대상이 실제로 손상되거나 죽은 것으로 제시될 때 `MOR`를 함께 검토한다.
- 해부 내용 `An`이나 인간 세부 `Hd`가 있다고 해서 자동으로 `MOR`가 되지 않는다.
- 인간 반응에서 `MOR`가 붙으면 `PHR` 가능성이 높아질 수 있지만, 그것만으로 자동 결정하지 않는다.

## 상호 참조

- [\[부호화/특수점수\] Special Scores](ref://scoring-input/special-score)
- [\[부호화/GHR-PHR\] PHR](ref://scoring-input/gphr/PHR)
- [\[부호화/특수점수\] AG](ref://scoring-input/special-score/AG)
- [\[해석/Ideation\] MOR](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation/MOR)
- [\[해석/Self Perception\] MOR](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception/MOR_self)

# [부호화/특수점수] PER

## 별칭/검색어

- PER
- personalized answers
- 개인화 반응
- 자기관여

## 핵심 정의

`PER`는 피검자가 반응을 정당화하거나 더 그럴듯하게 만들기 위해 자신의 지식, 경험, 익숙함을 직접 끌어올 때 붙이는 특수점수다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- "나는 예전에 그런 걸 봤다", "우리는 학교에서 배웠다"처럼 개인 경험이나 익숙함을 근거로 반응을 뒷받침하면 `PER`를 준다.
- 일인칭 대명사가 없더라도, 사적인 경험이나 배경지식을 끌어와 반응을 정당화하면 `PER`를 검토한다.
- 핵심은 대상을 본 것 자체보다, 그 지식이나 경험이 반응의 근거로 사용되고 있는가이다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- "내가 보기엔", "내 생각엔"처럼 말버릇처럼 붙는 표현만으로는 `PER`가 아니다.
- `I`, `my`, `we` 같은 인칭 표현이 들어 있어도 반응 정당화 기능이 없으면 `PER`를 주지 않는다.
- 개인적 설명이 반응과 직접 연결되지 않고 단순한 잡담에 가깝다면 `PER`가 아니다.
- `PER`는 내용 범주가 아니라 정당화 방식에 붙는 특수점수이므로, 내용 코드와 별도로 판단한다.

## 상호 참조

- [\[부호화/특수점수\] Special Scores](ref://scoring-input/special-score)
- [\[해석/Interpersonal\] PER](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/PER)
- [\[해석/Mediation\] Xu%](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/mediation/Xu_percent)

# [부호화/특수점수] PSV

## 별칭/검색어

- PSV
- perseveration
- 보속적 반응

## 핵심 정의

`PSV`는 이전 반응의 틀이나 대상을 반복해서 다시 쓰는 보속이 나타날 때 붙이는 특수점수다. 핵심은 단순한 수정이 아니라, 같은 반응이 경직되게 반복되는가이다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 한 카드 안에서 연속된 두 반응이 위치, 발달질, 결정인, 형태질, 내용 범주까지 사실상 같은 틀을 반복하면 `PSV`를 준다.
- 다른 카드에서라도 이전에 본 대상을 같은 대상으로 다시 확인하면 내용 보속으로 `PSV`를 검토한다.
- 여러 카드에 걸쳐 거의 기계적으로 같은 대상을 반복하면 기계적 보속으로 `PSV`를 준다.
- 세 유형은 구분해서 설명할 수 있지만, 부호는 모두 `PSV` 하나로 적는다.

- 단순히 더 적절한 대안을 고르는 수정 반응은 `PSV`가 아니다.

# [부호화/Z] Z

## 별칭/검색어

- Z
- 조직화 활동
- organizational activity

## 핵심 정의

`Z`는 반응에서 사용된 반점 요소들이 서로 의미 있게 통합될 때 부여하는 조직화 활동 부호군이다. `Z`가 성립하려면 형태 사용이 포함되어야 하며, 실제 채점 유형은 `ZW`, `ZA`, `ZD`, `ZS` 중 하나로 기록한다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 반응에 형태 사용이 포함되어 있어야 한다.
- 다음 중 최소 하나를 만족하면 `Z`를 검토한다.
- `W` 반응이면서 발달질 `+`, `v/+`, `o`를 포함하는 경우
- 두 개 이상 인접한 세부 영역을 의미 있게 통합하는 경우
- 두 개 이상 비인접 세부 영역을 의미 있게 통합하는 경우
- 공백이 다른 반점 부분과 의미 있게 통합되는 경우
- 한 반응이 두 가지 이상 준거를 동시에 만족하면, 그 카드에서 더 높은 가중치를 주는 `Z` 유형을 선택한다.
- 순수한 `C`, `T`, `Y`, `V` 반응처럼 형태 사용이 없는 반응은 `Z`로 채점하지 않는다.
- 질문 단계 정보는 `Z` 여부를 결정할 때 필요한 범위에서만 사용한다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- 단순히 여러 부분을 나열한 것만으로는 `Z`가 되지 않는다. 부분들 사이의 의미 있는 관계가 드러나야 한다.
- `W`를 썼다고 해서 자동으로 `ZW`가 되지 않는다. `DQ` 조건까지 확인해야 한다.
- `Wv` 반응에는 `Z`를 주지 않는다.
- `Z`는 위치(Location) 부호가 아니라 조직화 활동 부호다. `W`, `D`, `Dd`, `S`와 역할이 다르다.
- `ZS`는 공백이 실제로 대상이나 장면의 일부로 통합되었을 때만 준다. 단순한 윤곽 닫힘(closure)은 `ZS`가 아니다.

## 상호 참조

인접 규칙이나 연결된 해석 맥락이 필요할 때는 아래 문서를 함께 확인한다.

# [부호화/Z] ZA

## 별칭/검색어

- ZA
- adjacent detail organization
- 인접 부분 조직화

## 핵심 정의

`ZA`는 두 개 이상 인접한 세부 영역을 의미 있게 통합했을 때 부여하는 조직화 활동 유형이다. 전체 반응이 아니더라도, 서로 가까운 부분들이 하나의 장면이나 대상으로 묶여 있으면 `ZA`를 검토한다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 형태 사용이 포함되어 있어야 한다.
- 두 개 이상 인접한 세부 영역이 하나의 의미 있는 지각으로 통합되어 있어야 한다.
- 단순 병렬 나열이 아니라, 부분들 사이의 관계가 드러나야 한다.
- 경우에 따라 하나의 넓은 영역 안에서 부분을 나누어 조직적으로 통합한 반응도 `ZA`로 볼 수 있다.
- 카드별 `ZA` 가중치는 카드 번호에 따라 다르다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- 가까운 부분을 각각 따로 말한 것만으로는 `ZA`가 아니다.
- 물리적으로 붙어 있어도 지각된 대상들이 서로 떨어진 관계라면 `ZD`가 더 적절할 수 있다.
- 공백이 핵심 통합 요소라면 `ZS`를 먼저 검토한다.
- 같은 반응이 둘 이상의 `Z` 기준을 만족하면 카드별 더 높은 값의 유형을 선택한다.

## 상호 참조

# [부호화/Z] ZD

## 별칭/검색어

- ZD
- distant detail organization
- 원격 부분 조직화

## 핵심 정의

`ZD`는 두 개 이상 비인접 세부 영역을 의미 있게 통합했을 때 부여하는 조직화 활동 유형이다. 서로 떨어진 부분들을 하나의 장면이나 관계로 묶어 보는 방식이 핵심이다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 형태 사용이 포함되어 있어야 한다.
- 두 개 이상 비인접 세부 영역이 하나의 의미 있는 지각으로 연결되어야 한다.
- 반응 속 대상들이 서로 떨어져 지각되는 관계이면 `ZD`를 우선 검토한다.
- 카드별 `ZD` 가중치는 카드 번호에 따라 다르다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- 여러 부분이 등장해도 서로의 관계가 드러나지 않으면 `ZD`가 아니다.

- 공백이 통합 요소의 핵심이면 `ZS`를 먼저 검토한다.

# [부호화/Z] ZS

## 별칭/검색어

- ZS
- space organization
- 공백 조직화

## 핵심 정의

`ZS`는 공백이 다른 반점 부분과 의미 있게 통합되어 대상이나 장면의 일부로 기능할 때 부여하는 조직화 활동 유형이다. 핵심은 공백이 실제로 사용되었는지가 명시되는가이다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 형태 사용이 포함되어 있어야 한다.
- 공백과 하나 이상의 반점 부분이 함께 사용되어야 한다.
- 공백이 단순 배경이 아니라 대상이나 장면의 실제 구성 요소로 설명되어야 한다.
- 카드별 `ZS` 가중치는 카드 번호에 따라 다르다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- 공백을 둘러싸기만 한 반응이나 단순한 윤곽 닫힘은 `ZS`가 아니다.
- 카드 III와 X의 얼굴 반응처럼 공백이 자동으로 통합된 것처럼 보이는 경우는 과잉 채점에 주의한다.
- 공백이 실제로 흰 칠, 눈, 호수처럼 설명될 때에만 `ZS`를 준다.
- 공백만 단독 사용한 반응은 `ZS`가 아니고, 다른 반점 부분과의 통합이 필요하다.

## 상호 참조

# [부호화/Z] ZW

## 별칭/검색어

- ZW
- whole-blot organization
- 전체 반응 조직화

## 핵심 정의

`ZW`는 `W` 반응이면서 발달질이 `+`, `v/+`, `o` 중 하나일 때 부여하는 전체 반응 조직화 유형이다. 즉, 전체 반점을 형태적으로 조직해 사용했다는 점이 확인될 때의 `Z` 부호다.

## 채점/적용 조건

- 반응이 `W`여야 한다.
- 발달질이 `+`, `v/+`, `o` 중 하나여야 한다.
- 형태 사용이 포함되어 있어야 한다.
- 전체 반점이 의미 있는 하나의 조직화된 지각으로 사용되어야 한다.
- 카드별 `ZW` 가중치는 고정값이 아니라 카드 번호에 따라 다르다.
- 같은 반응이 다른 `Z` 준거도 동시에 만족하면, 카드별로 더 높은 가중치를 주는 유형을 선택한다.

## 주의사항/감별 기준

- `W`라고 해서 자동으로 `ZW`가 되는 것은 아니다. `Wv`는 `ZW`가 아니다.
- 전체를 썼더라도 의미 있는 조직화가 없으면 `Z`를 주지 않는다.
- 단순한 전체 명명은 `Location W`의 정보이고, `ZW`는 조직화 활동까지 확인된 경우다.
- 인접 세부 통합이나 공백 통합이 더 강하게 드러나면 `ZA`나 `ZS`가 최종 선택될 수 있다.

## 상호 참조

인접 규칙이나 연결된 해석 맥락이 필요할 때는 아래 문서를 함께 확인한다.

en.title: [Interpretation] result-interpretation
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation] result-interpretation

## Aliases

- result-interpretation
- interpretation
- structural summary interpretation
- result interpretation

## Definition

`result-interpretation` is the domain that takes the completed structural summary and organizes its clinical meaning.
It does not explain how to code a single response; it explains how already-calculated variables are read together.

## Interpretation

- Interpretation depends first on stable coding.
- The usual reading path is organized through `upper section`, `lower section`, and `special indices`.
- A single variable is rarely enough by itself; safer reading depends on patterns and combinations.
- When needed, structural interpretation should be checked against response sequence and content.
- Clinical interpretation should account for linguistic and cultural context while preserving the same Comprehensive System variables.

## Cautions

- This domain must stay separate from `scoring-input` documents.
- A high or low score does not automatically equal a diagnosis.
- Referral question, protocol length, and cultural context still matter when reading the profile.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Upper Section] Upper Section](ref://result-interpretation/upper-section)
- [[Interpretation/Lower Section] Lower Section](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices)
- [[Coding] scoring-input](ref://scoring-input)

en.title: [Interpretation/Lower Section] Lower Section
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Lower Section] Lower Section

## Aliases

- lower-section
- lower section
- lower section of structural summary

## Definition

`Lower Section` is the set of clusters where the structural summary is read as a functional pattern of resources, stress, ideation, affect, mediation, processing, interpersonal style, and self-perception.
If `Upper Section` works as the first screen, `Lower Section` is usually where clinical formulation becomes denser.

## Interpretation

- The reading flow usually follows `core -> ideation -> affect -> mediation -> processing -> interpersonal -> selfPerception`.
- A single number matters less than the way several indicators support or correct one another.
- This is where early signals from `Upper Section` are confirmed, qualified, or changed in meaning.

## Cautions

- `Lower Section` clusters influence one another; isolated reading increases the risk of overgeneralizing.
- Protocol length, defensiveness, cultural context, and situational stress can all change the weight of a variable.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation] result-interpretation](ref://result-interpretation)
- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Core] Core](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core)

[Cautions] Lower Section clusters influence one another; isolated reading increases the risk of overgeneralizing.

Protocol length, defensiveness, cultural context, and situational stress can all change the weight of a variable.

# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Affect] Affect

## Aliases

- affect
- emotion

## Definition

`Affect` gathers the variables used to read how emotion is experienced, modulated, and expressed in the protocol.
This section is usually reviewed through `FC:CF+C`, `Pure C`, `SumC / WSumC`, `Afr`, `S`, `Blends:R`, and `CP`.

## Interpretation

- `FC:CF+C` helps estimate whether feeling is more formally modulated or more directly discharged.
- `Pure C`, `SumC / WSumC`, and `CP` help show intensity and style of affective expression.
- `Afr` helps estimate how readily the person approaches or withdraws from emotionally loaded stimulation.
- `S` and `Blends:R` add information about opposition, complexity, and mixed affective states.

## Cautions

- Affect variables should not be read apart from `Core`, `Mediation`, and total protocol size.
- Mild elevation in one variable does not by itself prove affective dyscontrol.
- With low `R`, several affect ratios are less stable.

# [Interpretation/Affect] Afr

## Aliases

- Afr
- Affective Ratio

## Definition

`Afr` compares responses given to cards VIII, IX, and X with responses given to cards I through VII.
In interpretation, it is used to estimate how readily the person approaches or withdraws from stimulation with stronger affective or chromatic tone.

## Interpretation

- If `Afr` is low, there may be less readiness to approach emotionally loaded situations.
- If `Afr` is high, there may be greater openness to emotionally salient stimulation.
- Its meaning improves when it is read with `EB`, `Lambda`, and the broader style of affective expression.
- Under recent stress, `Afr` can temporarily drop.

## Cautions

- If total responses are low, the ratio can fluctuate too much.
- High `Afr` does not by itself mean healthy affective functioning, and low `Afr` does not automatically mean pathological avoidance.
- Card-by-card productivity differences should also be checked before drawing strong conclusions.

en.title: [Interpretation/Affect] Blends:R
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Affect] Blends:R

## Aliases

- Blends:R
- complexity index

## Definition

`Blends:R` expresses the proportion of responses that contain two or more determinants relative to total responses.
In affect, it helps estimate how much complexity and mixture of emotional states appears in experience.

## Interpretation

- If the ratio is high, there may be greater affective complexity and more emotional layers active at the same time.
- If it is low, experience may appear simpler, less nuanced, or less integrated.
- Both the ratio and total `R` should be checked, because a highly productive protocol can lower the ratio.

## Cautions

- A high ratio does not automatically mean healthy flexibility; it can also accompany tension or overload.
- A low ratio does not necessarily imply emotional poverty, especially when `R` is small or `Lambda` is high.
- Color-shading blends deserve added attention because they can signal mixed affect and distress.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Affect] CP

## Aliases

- CP
- color projection

## Definition

`CP` in affect is used to read attribution of color or emotional tone to a field that would not ordinarily contain it.
It is reviewed as a sign that affect is imposing itself on perception in an unusual way.

## Interpretation

- If `CP` appears, there may be a tendency to load more neutral contexts with emotion.
- Because it is rare, even a single case deserves clinical attention.
- It is often useful to see whether it appears together with shading determinants or other markers of tension.

## Cautions

- `CP` is not the same as `Pure C`, `CF`, or `C`.
- The special-score coding should be confirmed before interpretation.
- Its rarity gives it clinical weight, but it is not enough by itself for a broad conclusion.

en.title: [Interpretation/Affect] FC:CF+C
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Affect] FC:CF+C

## Aliases

- FC:CF+C
- affect ratio
- form-color ratio
- color-form ratio

## Definition

`FC:CF+C` is displayed as `FC : (CF + C + Cn)`, with each occurrence counted equally. It expresses how form and color are combined across chromatic color responses.
In interpretation, it helps estimate whether emotion is more formally modulated or more directly discharged.

## Interpretation

- If `FC` dominates, affective expression is usually more controlled and shaped by formal modulation.
- If `CF+C` dominates, feeling may be expressed more directly, immediately, or with less modulation.
- A more balanced pattern suggests a mix of control and direct expression.
- This ratio says more about style of emotional expression than about total emotional quantity.

## Cautions

- When there are only a few color responses, the ratio is less stable.
- A stronger `CF+C` side should not by itself be treated as proof of pathology or impulsive acting out.
- `Pure C` may show a more direct affective discharge that is not fully captured by this ratio.
- `Cn` is included only on the displayed ratio's right side. It is excluded from `WSumC`, the separate S-CON comparison `CF+C > FC`, and the Color-Shading blend count.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Affect] Pure C
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Affect] Pure C

## Aliases

- Pure C
- pure color

## Definition

`Pure C` is the frequency of color responses that do not have formal support.
In interpretation, it is used as a sign of more direct affective expression that is less shaped by structure or formal control.

## Interpretation

- If `Pure C` appears, there may be moments when feeling is expressed more immediately.
- Repeated `Pure C` suggests that affect can override formal organization in the response.
- In adult protocols, even a small amount deserves attention because the base rate is usually low.

## Cautions

- `Pure C` does not by itself equal pathological impulsivity.
- It should be distinguished from `CF`, `FC`, and `CP`.
- If there were few opportunities for chromatic responses, absence of `Pure C` does not mean absence of affect.

# [Interpretation/Affect] S

## Aliases

- S
- white space affect

## Definition

`S` in affect refers to the frequency of responses that use white space with emotional interpretive value.
It is reviewed as a possible sign of opposition, self-assertion, tension, or distance from the stimulus field.

## Interpretation

- If `S` is high, there may be more tendency to respond from opposition, negativism, or defensive self-assertion.
- In some protocols it can also reflect anger, internal pressure, or a need to mark distance.
- Not every white-space response is hostility; some cases reflect exploratory style or perceptual searching.

## Cautions

- It should not be confused with `S` in the upper section or with `S-%` in mediation.
- A small number of cases is not enough to define a stable oppositional style.
- It is useful to see whether white-space use appears together with `AG`, `CP`, or broader tension markers.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Affect] Affect](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/affect)

en.title: [Interpretation/Affect] SumC / WSumC
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Affect] SumC / WSumC

## Aliases

- SumC
- WSumC
- weighted sum color

## Definition

`SumC / WSumC` summarizes the total amount of chromatic color responses and their weighted impact.
In interpretation, `WSumC` is usually more useful because it reflects not only how many color responses appeared, but also how much direct affective load they carry.

## Interpretation

- If `WSumC` is high, affective activation may occupy a larger place in experience and decision-making.
- Comparing `SumC` with `WSumC` helps distinguish simple amount of color from stronger clinical weight of chromatic responses.
- `WSumC` also enters core variables such as `EB`, so it influences the protocol's broader balance.

## Cautions

- A high `WSumC` does not automatically mean healthy affective expression or dyscontrol.
- `Cn` is not counted in `WSumC`, so color naming should not be merged with true chromatic responses.
- It should be separated from `SumCprime`, which refers to achromatic color rather than chromatic color.

en.title: [Interpretation/Lower Section/Core] Core
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Core] Core

## Aliases

- core
- basic resources and stress
- core cluster

## Definition

`Core` is the cluster where the protocol's basic resources, current level of demand, coping balance, and tension load are reviewed together.
This is where `R`, `Lambda`, `EB`, `EA`, `eb`, `es`, `D`, `AdjD`, and the tension variables such as `m`, `SumCprime`, `SumT`, `SumV`, and `SumY` are read as a set.

## Interpretation

- `R` helps determine whether the protocol offers enough material for stable interpretation.
- `Lambda` shows the degree of simplification or economy in processing.
- `EB`, `EA`, `eb`, `es`, `D`, and `AdjD` help estimate resources, demand, and coping balance.
- `FM`, `m`, `SumCprime`, `SumT`, `SumV`, and `SumY` qualify the nature of tension and internal burden.

## Cautions

- `Core` variables influence one another; a single number can be misleading.
- In short protocols or protocols with very high `Lambda`, several values in the cluster can look reduced or distorted.

en.title: [Interpretation/Core] AdjD
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] AdjD

## Aliases

- AdjD
- Adjusted D
- adjusted D score

## Definition

`AdjD` is not the raw difference itself. First calculate `EA - AdjEs`, then apply the same scaled conversion used for D: raw differences from `-2.5` through `+2.5` yield `0`, and each additional `2.5` points changes AdjD by one unit with the same sign. The sequence continues beyond the usual printed `-5` to `+5` table when needed.

It works as a more stable estimate of control margin because `AdjEs` removes all but one `m` and one `Y` from `es`, reducing part of the situational overload represented by those determinants.

## Interpretation

- `AdjD = 0` usually suggests approximate balance after the more reactive burden has been corrected.
- `AdjD < 0` suggests a more persistent or less purely situational form of overload.
- If `D` looks clearly worse than `AdjD`, part of the current distress may be amplified by immediate situational pressure.
- `AdjD` is often more useful than `D` when estimating baseline vulnerability to stress.

## Cautions

- `AdjD` should not be read as a fixed trait.
- A nonnegative `AdjD` does not rule out breakdown under strong external pressure.
- The gap between `D` and `AdjD` is clinically important because it helps separate current load from more sustained load.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Core] AdjEs
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] AdjEs

## Aliases

- AdjEs
- Adjusted es
- adjusted experienced stimulation

## Definition

`AdjEs` is a corrected form of `es`.
It estimates how much burden remains after part of the weight from `m` and `Y` has been adjusted out.

## Interpretation

- High `AdjEs` suggests that the burden is not only momentary and may be more sustained.
- If `es` is high but `AdjEs` drops clearly, a meaningful part of the current strain may be tied to situational stress.
- `AdjEs` is mainly useful because it helps calculate and contextualize `AdjD`.
- It is a correction variable, not a diagnostic label by itself.

## Cautions

- `AdjEs` does not replace `es`; both need to be compared.
- A high value does not by itself specify the exact source of distress.
- The clinician should still check whether the burden is being driven mainly by `m`, `Y`, or other load components.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Core] D
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] D

## Aliases

- D
- D score
- current stress tolerance

## Definition

`D` is not the raw difference itself. First calculate `EA - es`, then convert that raw difference to the scaled D score. A raw difference from `-2.5` through `+2.5` yields `D = 0`; beyond that interval, D changes by one unit for each additional `2.5` raw-score points, preserving the sign. The same conversion rule continues beyond the usual printed `-5` to `+5` table when an extreme protocol requires it.

It summarizes whether available resources are enough to manage the current level of demand without clear overload.

## Interpretation

- `D = 0` usually suggests approximate balance between resources and current demand.
- `D > 0` suggests adaptive margin and less immediate risk of becoming overwhelmed by the current situation.
- `D < 0` suggests that current demand exceeds available resources and may be associated with tension, irritability, or lower frustration tolerance.
- `D` is especially sensitive to current conditions, so it can move with recent situational stress.

## Cautions

- `D = 0` does not automatically mean sound adjustment; a simplified or defensive protocol can look balanced.
- `D > 0` does not by itself prove stable overall strength.
- `D < 0` points to current overload, but the comparison with `AdjD` is needed to judge whether the strain is more situational or more persistent.

en.title: [Interpretation/Core] EA
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] EA

## Aliases

- EA
- Experience Actual
- available resources

## Definition

`EA` is the index of available resources derived from the components of `EB`.
It indicates how much effective capacity the person has to handle ordinary demands and modulate current experience.

## Interpretation

- Adequate `EA` suggests enough basic resources for everyday demands.
- Low `EA` may indicate limited resources for regulating tension and meeting demands.
- Sufficient `EA` does not by itself guarantee adaptation; it has to be compared with the burden represented by `es`.
- `EA` is one of the main bases for reading `D` and `AdjD`.

## Cautions

- If `EA` looks sufficient but `EBPer` is very rigid or `es` is very high, actual functioning may still be unstable.
- In short protocols or protocols with high `Lambda`, the number can underestimate or oversimplify the real picture.
- `EA` refers to resources that are potentially available, not to perfect use of those resources in every situation.

## Cross References

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] EB

## Aliases

- EB
- Erlebnistypus
- Experience Balance
- experiential balance

## Definition

`EB` is the ratio `M : WSumC`.
It shows whether the person tends to rely more on ideational, reflective elaboration or more on affective modulation and emotional response when dealing with problems.

## Interpretation

- If `M` predominates, the style is usually described as more `introversive`.
- If `WSumC` predominates, the style is usually described as more `extratensive`.
- If there is a clear but not extreme direction, there may be a preferred style with some flexibility.
- If no clear direction appears, the style is usually described as `ambitent`, suggesting less consistency in coping direction.

## Cautions

- A marked direction does not automatically equal health or pathology.
- If the difference is very large, `EBPer` should also be checked.
- In short protocols, protocols with high `Lambda`, or protocols with low `EA`, `EB` can look more rigid or emptier than it actually is.

en.title: [Interpretation/Core] EBPer
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] EBPer

## Aliases

- EBPer
- EB Pervasive
- EB pervasiveness

## Definition

`EBPer` is the ratio between the larger and smaller sides of `EB`.
It is interpreted only when `EB` has a clear direction, and it helps estimate how fixed or dominant that coping preference is.

It is calculated only when all eligibility conditions are met: `EA >= 4.0`, `Lambda < 1.0`, and the absolute difference between the two sides of `EB` is at least `2.0` when `EA` is from `4.0` through `10.0`, or at least `2.5` when `EA > 10.0`. Both sides must be greater than zero so that the larger side can be divided by the smaller side. Otherwise, `EBPer` is not reported.

## Interpretation

- Lower `EBPer` suggests that a preferred style exists but still keeps some flexibility.
- High `EBPer` indicates that the `introversive` or `extratensive` direction becomes more rigid or dominant.
- In that case, the person may rely too heavily on a preferred channel and lose flexibility.

## Cautions

- `EBPer` is not interpreted if `EB` has no clear direction.
- Crossing the cut-off does not by itself mean pathology; it describes reduced flexibility.
- If `EA` is very low or the protocol is short, the ratio may look more extreme than it really is.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] FM

## Aliases

- FM
- animal movement total
- total animal movement

## Definition

`FM` is the total number of animal movement responses.
In `core`, it usually acts as a component on the left side of `eb`, reflecting need tension, pressure for discharge, and motivational demand that is not yet fully elaborated.

## Interpretation

- Moderate `FM` can suggest that needs and inner pressures are present and pushing behavior.
- High `FM` can suggest greater pressure from unsatisfied needs, drives, or discharge demands.
- `FM` contributes to `eb` and, together with `m`, can raise `es`.
- Its meaning becomes clearer when compared with `m`, `D`, and `AdjD`.

## Cautions

- High `FM` does not by itself prove openly disorganized impulse control.
- `FM` should not be confused with `M`; here it points to more basic or less integrated pressure rather than mature ideational elaboration.
- Its clinical weight changes according to the balance with `m`, `es`, `D`, and `AdjD`.

en.title: [Interpretation/Core] Lambda
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] Lambda

## Aliases

- Lambda
- L
- lambda

## Definition

`Lambda` is the ratio between pure-form responses and the rest of the responses.
In interpretation it is used as an indicator of how much the protocol simplifies, economizes, or restricts processing.

## Interpretation

- High `Lambda` often marks a simpler, more economical, or more defensive style.
- In protocols of sufficient length, high `Lambda` may accompany avoidance, field reduction, or simplified handling of the stimulus.
- Very low `Lambda` may be associated with greater complexity, but also with overinclusion or excessive openness.

## Cautions

- If `R` is low, high `Lambda` may reflect guardedness more than a stable style.
- Low `Lambda` is not automatically a strength; if resources are weak, it may coexist with inefficiency.
- `Zd`, `W:D:Dd`, `EB`, `EA`, `D`, and `AdjD` should be reviewed with it.

# [Interpretation/Core] R

## Aliases

- R
- response total
- total number of responses

## Definition

`R` is the total number of responses in the protocol.
In interpretation it functions first as an indicator of range, productivity, and record adequacy.

## Interpretation

- Very low `R` requires great caution in reading the protocol.
- A sufficient `R` gives a more stable basis for interpreting the rest of the structural summary.
- High `R` is not automatically a strength; it may also accompany expansiveness or overproduction.

## Cautions

- Low `R` may reflect defensiveness, withdrawal, fatigue, situational anxiety, or problems in the test relationship.
- High `R` does not by itself imply adaptive richness.
- The meaning of `R` changes with `Lambda`, `DQ`, and test behavior.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Core] SumCprime

## Aliases

- SumCprime
- SumC'
- achromatic sum

## Definition

`SumCprime` is the sum of the achromatic determinants `FC'`, `C'F`, and `C'`.
In `core`, it usually indicates the weight of dysphoric discomfort, unpleasant affect, or a more internalized and constricted emotional tone.

## Interpretation

- High `SumCprime` can suggest greater dysphoria, inner discomfort, or painful affect that is not being expressed openly.
- This value contributes to the shading side of `eb` and can increase `es`.
- Its meaning becomes clearer when compared with `SumC / WSumC`, because that contrast helps distinguish internalized distress from more openly expressed emotion.
- If `AdjD` falls while `SumCprime` rises, more sustained discomfort may be carrying greater weight.

## Cautions

- High `SumCprime` does not by itself prove clinical depression.
- Low `SumCprime` does not rule out distress, because some people restrict or simplify affective expression in the protocol.
- It is useful to review its relation to `Afr`, `SumShd`, and `WSumC`.

## Cross References

# [Interpretation/Core] SumT

## Aliases

- SumT
- texture total
- total texture

## Definition

`SumT` is the sum of texture determinants.
In `core`, it usually indicates how much the need for closeness, comfort, or protective contact is contributing to the current burden.

## Interpretation

- High `SumT` can suggest that the need for emotional proximity or support is active as part of the current load.
- `SumT` belongs to the shading side of `eb` and can increase `es`.
- In `core`, it is read first as a need or burden variable; the more relational form of that need is better explored in the interpersonal domain.
- Its meaning changes with the larger context of `eb`, `es`, and available resources.

## Cautions

- High `SumT` does not automatically mean relational warmth or good attachment capacity.
- `SumT = 0` does not prove total absence of attachment or closeness needs.
- It is useful to separate the current-burden reading in `core` from the relational-style reading in `interpersonal`.

# [Interpretation/Core] SumV

## Aliases

- SumV
- vista total
- total vista

## Definition

`SumV` is the sum of vista determinants.
In `core`, it usually indicates how much self-criticism, dissatisfaction with the self, or self-evaluative discomfort is contributing to current strain.

## Interpretation

- High `SumV` can suggest greater self-criticism, regret, or dissatisfaction with oneself.
- In `core`, it is read as part of current burden; in `selfPerception`, it is examined more specifically as part of self-concept.
- `SumV` can contribute to `es` and reduce adaptive margin when it combines with other burden indicators.
- Its meaning becomes clearer when reviewed with other indicators of self-evaluation and dysphoria.

## Cautions

- High `SumV` does not by itself mean self-hatred or a fixed personality trait.
- A value of `0` does not rule out self-criticism if it is expressed in other ways.
- It is important to separate the current-burden reading in `core` from the broader structural reading in `selfPerception`.

# [Interpretation/Core] SumY

## Aliases

- SumY
- diffuse shading total
- total diffuse shading

## Definition

`SumY` is the sum of diffuse shading determinants.
In `core`, it usually reflects vague distress, difficult-to-modulate tension, or a sense of burden that feels diffuse and less controllable.

## Interpretation

- High `SumY` can suggest greater diffuse anxiety, emotional pressure, or a sense of overload.
- `SumY` increases the shading side of `eb` and can raise `es`.
- It is usually associated more with reactive or situational distress than with a complete structural formulation.
- Its meaning becomes clearer when compared with `m`, `D`, and `AdjEs`.

## Cautions

- High `SumY` does not by itself prove trauma, hopelessness, or a specific diagnosis.
- `SumY = 0` does not rule out distress, because other shading variables or `m` may be carrying the burden.
- It is best kept as a state-oriented indicator rather than a fixed trait label.

# [Interpretation/Core] eb

## Aliases

- eb
- Experience Base
- experienced-stimulation base

## Definition

`eb` is the ratio `FM + m : SumShd`.
It describes the composition of current demand: whether the burden is weighted more by unmet-needs tension and active unrest, or more by diffuse discomfort, shading, and dysphoric affect.

## Interpretation

- If `FM + m` predominates, current demand may lean toward active tension, unrest, or pressure around impulse and need.
- If `SumShd` predominates, diffuse discomfort, affective strain, or internal uneasiness may weigh more heavily.
- `eb` describes the composition of demand; it is not the same as the total amount of burden.
- It prepares the way for reading `es`, `D`, `AdjEs`, and `AdjD`.

## Cautions

- `eb` is a ratio, not a total magnitude.
- It is important to review the specific components that create it: `FM`, `m`, `C'`, `T`, `V`, and `Y`.
- In short protocols, the ratio may look exaggerated or unstable.

# [Interpretation/Core] es

## Aliases

- es
- Experienced Stimulations
- current demand load

## Definition

`es` is the sum of the components that make up `eb`.
It represents the total magnitude of current demand or internal burden being registered in the protocol.

## Interpretation

- High `es` suggests many active internal demands and a higher tension load.
- `es` in a moderate range suggests that current demand is not clearly overwhelming the system.
- Low `es` does not automatically mean absence of distress; it can also reflect minimization or defensive reduction.
- Its comparison with `EA` is central for reading `D` and `AdjD`.

## Cautions

- High `es` indicates burden, but it does not by itself determine whether that burden is temporary or chronic.
- Low `es` with low `EA` may speak more to general scarcity than to calmness.
- `eb` should be reviewed to see what kind of demand makes up the total.

# [Interpretation/Core] m

## Aliases

- m
- inanimate movement total
- total inanimate movement

## Definition

`m` is the total number of inanimate movement responses.
In `core`, it is usually read as an indicator of reactive tension, feeling pushed by external forces, or difficult-to-control situational worry.

## Interpretation

- `m = 0` suggests that this kind of reactive tension is not strongly represented in the protocol.
- High `m` can be associated with pressure, helplessness, intrusive worry, or heavy situational load.
- `m` usually carries a more reactive and less integrated tone than `FM`.
- `m` weighs into `AdjEs` and helps explain why `D` can drop under recent stress.

## Cautions

- High `m` does not by itself mean total passivity or a specific disorder.
- The comparison between `D` and `AdjD` is important for separating situational strain from a more sustained pattern.
- `m` should be read with `Y` and `es`, not as an isolated value.

# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Ideation] Ideation

## Aliases

- Ideation
- ideation
- thinking

## Definition

`Ideation` is the group of variables used to read the direction of thought, the organization of representations, and the presence of cognitive peculiarities or slippage.
In this section, `a:p`, `Ma:Mp`, `2AB+Art+Ay`, `MOR`, `Sum6`, `Lv2`, `WSum6`, `M-`, and `Mnone` are reviewed together.

## Interpretation

- `a:p` and `Ma:Mp` help show whether mental activity leans more toward initiative or passivity.
- `2AB+Art+Ay` shows how much thought shifts toward abstract, artificial, or less immediate formulations.
- `MOR` adds the weight of damage, failure, deterioration, or loss within ideational content.
- `Sum6`, `Lv2`, and `WSum6` summarize the magnitude of cognitive peculiarities.
- `M-` and `Mnone` help show how well thought linked to human movement is organized.

## Cautions

- This group should not be read without considering protocol quality and the context of `Mediation` and `Processing`.
- A mildly elevated single variable is not enough to conclude major ideational distortion.
- When `M` is very scarce, some ratios or contrasts lose stability.

# [Interpretation/Ideation] Lv2

## Aliases

- Lv2
- Level 2 special scores
- level 2 markers

## Definition

`Lv2` shows how many level-2 special scores appear in the protocol.
In interpretation, it indicates how much weight the more severe cognitive peculiarities carry within thought.

## Interpretation

- If `Lv2 = 0`, no level-2 markers appear in the special-score set.
- If there is only one occurrence, the context should be checked carefully before overstating it.
- If several level-2 occurrences appear, the likelihood of more marked ideational disorganization or distortion increases.

## Cautions

- `Lv2` carries more weight because of severity than because of simple frequency.
- It is not enough by itself to conclude a thought disorder; it should be read with `WSum6`, `M-`, `PTI`, and mediation variables.
- `CONTAM` also counts as level 2, but its structure is different from `DV2`, `DR2`, `INCOM2`, or `FABCOM2`.

[Title] [Interpretation/Ideation] Lv2
[Aliases] Lv2, Level 2 special scores, level 2 markers
[Definition] Lv2 shows how many level-2 special scores appear in the protocol.
In interpretation, it indicates how much weight the more severe cognitive peculiarities carry within thought.
[Interpretation] If Lv2 = 0, no level-2 markers appear in the special-score set.

If there is only one occurrence, the context should be checked carefully before overstating it.

If several level-2 occurrences appear, the likelihood of more marked ideational disorganization or distortion increases.
[Cautions] Lv2 carries more weight because of severity than because of simple frequency.

It is not enough by itself to conclude a thought disorder; it should be read with WSum6, M-, PTI, and mediation variables.

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] MOR
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] MOR

## Aliases

- MOR
- morbid ideation
- morbid content tone

## Definition

`MOR` shows how often themes of damage, loss, defect, ruin, failure, or deterioration appear in thought.
In the ideation area, it helps show how much mental content is colored by negative or damaged imagery.

## Interpretation

- High `MOR` can suggest more frequent thought centered on deterioration, damage, loss, or failure.
- It can be associated with a more pessimistic cognitive tone or heavier expectation of negative outcomes.
- When these themes appear in human or self-referential content, the reading may move closer to the self-perception domain.
- Its value increases when it is integrated with other indicators of negative affect or ideational quality.

## Cautions

- High `MOR` does not by itself confirm depression, trauma, or a specific disorder.
- It is important to distinguish a single unpleasant image from a consistent morbid tone in thought.
- A low value does not guarantee absence of self-criticism or hopelessness.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] M-
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] M-

## Aliases

- M-
- minus human movement
- poor form human movement

## Definition

`M-` indicates human movement responses with minus form quality.
In interpretation, it is used as a sign that imagined human activity is distorted, poorly anchored in shared reality, or less accurately organized.

## Interpretation

- If `M-` appears, human representations may show less precise or less reality-based thinking.
- If it accumulates with `Lv2` or `WSum6`, concern about ideational disorganization increases.
- It can point to odd human fantasy, distorted reading of other people, or less integrated mental elaboration.

## Cautions

- Not every unusual `M` response is `M-`; the `M` coding and form quality both have to be confirmed first.
- A single `M-` is not enough to define a thought disorder.
- Its weight changes greatly depending on how it combines with `Mnone`, `PTI`, mediation, and processing.

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] Ma:Mp
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] Ma:Mp

## Aliases

- Ma:Mp
- active:passive human movement
- human movement active:passive

## Definition

`Ma:Mp` expresses the ratio between active and passive human movement within `M` responses.
It helps show whether imagined human activity tends to be represented as acting and intervening or as waiting, receiving, or being acted upon.

## Interpretation

- If `Mp` exceeds `Ma`, human ideation may more often represent passivity, waiting, or receptivity.
- If `Ma` predominates, human ideation may lean more toward initiative, intervention, or directing action.
- When the ratio is balanced, human representations are not strongly pulled toward one pole.
- Its meaning becomes more useful when integrated with the quality of `M`.

## Cautions

- If the number of `M` responses is very low, the ratio loses stability.
- Predominant `Mp` does not by itself imply fragility, and predominant `Ma` does not by itself imply positive adjustment.
- The quality of ideation still has to be checked through `M-` and `Mnone`.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Ideation] Ideation](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation)

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] Mnone
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] Mnone

## Aliases

- Mnone
- formless human movement
- human movement without form

## Definition

`Mnone` indicates human movement responses that do not have enough form to support a regular `M` interpretation.
In interpretation, it functions as a sign that human fantasy or imagined human activity is present but weakly structured.

## Interpretation

- If `Mnone` appears, human representations may be vague, weakly organized, or only loosely anchored in form.
- It can point to human imagination that is present but not clearly shaped enough to carry the same weight as well-formed `M`.
- If it appears with `M-`, `WSum6`, or `SCON`, concern about ideational vulnerability rises.

## Cautions

- `Mnone` is not the same as `M-`; `Mnone` lacks sufficient form, while `M-` has minus form quality.
- A single `Mnone` should not be treated as proof of major ideational disturbance.
- The `M` coding should be checked first so that the response is not misclassified.

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] Sum6
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] Sum6

## Aliases

- Sum6
- sum of six special scores
- six special scores total

## Definition

`Sum6` is the simple total of responses counted within the six thought-related special scores.
It is used to estimate how often cognitive oddities, verbal deviations, or problematic ideational combinations appear in the protocol.

## Interpretation

- High `Sum6` suggests a greater frequency of cognitive peculiarities within the protocol.
- It is a quantity index, not a severity judgment by itself.
- In adult protocols, a clearly elevated value calls for closer review of thought organization.
- Its meaning becomes more precise when compared with `Lv2` and `WSum6`.

## Cautions

- If `R` is high, part of the increase may simply reflect more chances to accumulate special scores.
- High `Sum6` with mostly level-1 responses does not carry the same weight as a profile with multiple level-2 responses.
- If `Lv2`, `CONTAM`, or `M-` are also present, interpretation should become more cautious.

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] WSum6
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] WSum6

## Aliases

- WSum6
- Weighted Sum6
- weighted six special scores

## Definition

`WSum6` is the weighted sum of the six thought-related special scores.
It not only counts how many peculiarities appear, but also how much clinical weight they carry according to severity.

## Interpretation

- The higher `WSum6` is, the greater the overall weight of cognitive distortion or peculiarity.
- Two protocols with similar `Sum6` can still differ if one contains more severe indicators.
- In adult protocols, a high `WSum6` deserves closer review of thought consistency and disorganization risk.

## Cautions

- `WSum6` does not replace checking which specific special scores are present.
- It is useful to see whether the increase comes from `Lv2`, `CONTAM`, or several smaller indicators accumulating.
- It should be read with `M-`, `PTI`, mediation, and processing rather than as an isolated marker.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Ideation] Ideation](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation)

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] 2AB+Art+Ay
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] 2AB+Art+Ay

## Aliases

- 2AB+Art+Ay
- intellectualizing composite
- 2AB Art Ay

## Definition

`2AB+Art+Ay` combines twice `AB` with `Art` and `Ay`.
It is used to estimate how often thought moves away from direct experience and shifts toward more abstract, artificial, or stylized formulations.

## Interpretation

- A high value can suggest a tendency to gain distance from immediate experience through abstraction, stylization, or more intellectualized formulation.
- In some protocols this elevation may reflect a defensive resource, while in others it may reflect a more conceptual cognitive style.
- Its meaning changes according to the overall quality of thought and the rest of the ideation indicators.
- It is useful to check whether it appears alongside other signs of affective thinning or ideational strangeness.

## Cautions

- A high value should not automatically be mistaken for thought disorder.
- `Art` and `Ay` can also be influenced by cultural interests, expressive style, or symbolic preferences.
- `AB` is a special score, while `Art` and `Ay` are contents, so the source of the elevation should be checked carefully.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Ideation] Ideation](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation)

en.title: [Interpretation/Ideation] a:p
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Ideation] a:p

## Aliases

- a:p
- a_p
- active:passive

## Definition

`a:p` summarizes the ratio between active and passive movement responses.
It is used to estimate whether mental activity leans more toward initiative and intervention or toward waiting, receptivity, and reaction.

## Interpretation

- If `p` clearly outweighs `a`, ideation may lean more toward waiting, receptivity, or a less directive stance.
- If `a` predominates, there may be more tendency to intervene, act, or push situations through thought.
- The value is more interpretable when there are enough movement responses.
- It is useful to read it together with `Ma:Mp` so the broader movement pattern can be separated from specifically human movement.

## Cautions

- With very few movement responses, small differences can be unstable.
- Predominant `p` does not by itself mean pathological submission, and predominant `a` does not by itself mean healthy adjustment.
- In interpersonal reading, this ratio should be kept separate from the `a:p` used in the interpersonal domain.

en.title: [Interpretation/Lower Section/Interpersonal] Interpersonal
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Interpersonal] Interpersonal

## Aliases

- interpersonal
- interpersonal relations
- relational style

## Definition

`Interpersonal` gathers the variables that help read how the person imagines, seeks, fears, or organizes contact with other people.
In this cluster, the main focus is on `COP`, `AG`, `GHR:PHR`, `a:p`, `Food`, `SumT`, human content, and interpersonal isolation.

## Interpretation

- `COP` and `AG` show whether interpersonal scenes are imagined more cooperatively or more conflictually.
- `GHR:PHR` is a descriptive frequency ratio of Good Human Representations to Poor Human Representations. It does not by itself establish interpersonal functioning.
- `SumT_inter` and `Food` help estimate needs for closeness, support, or dependency.
- `HumanCont` and `PureH` show how much human representation is present in the record.
- `PER` and `ISO_Index` add information about self-reference, distance, and social isolation.

## Cautions

- No interpersonal variable should be read by itself.
- High human content does not automatically mean healthy relationships.
- Interpersonal style changes meaning depending on affect, mediation, and ideation.

## Cautions

- This cluster gives direction about expectations and organization of relatedness, not a complete explanation of relational life.
- It should be integrated with `Core`, `Affect`, `Ideation`, and `Self Perception`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `SumT`
- `a:p`
- `H ratio`
- `CDI`
- `DEPI`

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] AG
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] AG

## Aliases

- AG
- aggressive movement
- aggressive imagery

## Definition

`AG` shows how often the record represents interpersonal scenes in aggressive, hostile, or confrontational terms.
In interpretation, it is used to read whether relatedness is more easily organized around conflict or threat.

## Interpretation

- If `AG` is high, there may be a greater tendency to imagine interpersonal contact as tense, aggressive, or confrontational.
- The absence of `AG` does not remove all conflict, but it lowers the weight of openly aggressive scenes.
- `AG` describes a way of representing relatedness, not direct proof of violent behavior.
- Reading it with `COP` helps distinguish predominantly cooperative records from more ambivalent or conflictual ones.

## Cautions

- `AG` should not be translated immediately into behavioral risk.
- Its meaning changes if it appears with `MOR`, `S_aff`, or `PHR`.
- It is important to review whether aggression appears more as defense, expectation, or general imagined tone.

## Cautions

- `AG` is only one piece of interpersonal style.
- It should be read with `COP`, `ISO_Index`, `SumT_inter`, `MOR`, and `PHR`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `COP`
- `PHR`
- `S`
- `MOR`
- `ISO_Index`

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] COP
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] COP

## Aliases

- COP
- cooperative movement
- cooperative imagery

## Definition

`COP` shows how often the record includes cooperative or mutually coordinated interpersonal scenes.
In interpretation, it works as a clue to how easily relatedness is imagined in terms of support, coordination, or reciprocity.

## Interpretation

- If `COP` appears, there is often more expectation of cooperative exchange or more readiness to imagine supportive relationships.
- If `COP` is very low or absent, the record may lean less toward cooperative scenes.
- The value does not describe perfect social skill; it describes the kind of relational organization imagined most easily.
- Comparing it with `AG` helps show whether the dominant interpersonal tone is cooperative, conflictual, or mixed.

## Cautions

- High `COP` does not guarantee healthy or stable real relationships.
- Low `COP` does not automatically mean pathology.
- `COP` and `AG` can coexist in the same protocol.

## Cautions

- `COP` offers only one sign about imagined relational structure.
- It should be read with `SumT_inter`, `HumanCont`, `ISO_Index`, and `GHR/PHR`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `AG`
- `HumanCont`
- `SumT_inter`
- `ISO_Index`
- `GHR`

# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Food

## Aliases

- Food
- food content
- dependency imagery

## Definition

`Food` shows how much food content appears when it is read on the interpersonal level.
In interpretation, it is used as a secondary indicator of need for care, support, or dependency in relatedness.

## Interpretation

- In adults, the presence of `Food` usually invites review of needs for support or relational gratification.
- If it appears together with `SumT_inter`, the search for closeness may look stronger.
- The variable is not mainly about literal hunger; it is more often used as a symbolic clue to needing to be fed or cared for.

## Cautions

- In child protocols, its frequency may carry different weight than it does in adults.
- `Food = 1` is not enough to conclude intense dependency.
- Coding `Fd` should not be confused with automatic interpretation of interpersonal deprivation.

## Cautions

- `Food` is a supplementary variable.
- It should be read with `SumT_inter`, `COP`, `ISO_Index`, and `CDI`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `SumT_inter`
- `SumT`
- `COP`
- `ISO_Index`
- `CDI`

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Human Content
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Human Content

## Aliases

- HumanCont
- Human Content
- total human content

## Definition

`HumanCont` summarizes how much human content appears in the record when `H + (H) + Hd + (Hd)` are added together.
At the interpersonal level, it helps estimate how much weight people and human themes carry in the person's relational world.

## Interpretation

- If `HumanCont` is high, there is usually more attention to people, human scenes, or interpersonal exchange.
- If it is low, there may be less interest in human material, more relational distance, or a focus on nonpersonal objects and features.
- The variable shows amount of human representation, not its quality.
- To judge whether those representations are more integrated or more distorted, it is useful to review `PureH`, `GHR`, and `PHR`.

## Cautions

- `HumanCont` does not include `Hx`.
- A high value does not automatically mean healthy or empathic relationships.
- A low value alone is not enough to conclude chronic isolation.

## Cautions

- This variable reflects the weight of human themes, not the full form of relatedness.
- It should be read with `PureH`, `GHR`, `PHR`, and `H ratio`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `PureH`
- `GHR`
- `PHR`
- `H ratio`
- `ISO_Index`

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Isolation Index
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Isolation Index

## Aliases

- ISO Index
- Isolation Index
- Isolate/R
- isolation ratio

## Definition

`ISO_Index` is the ratio `(Bt + 2Cl + Ge + Ls + 2Na) / R`.
In interpretation, it helps estimate how much the record is organized around distance, social withdrawal, or limited interpersonal participation.

## Interpretation

- If the index rises above `.24` or `.25`, it is worth reviewing hypotheses about social distance or interpersonal withdrawal more carefully.
- A value near `1/3` or higher increases concern about meaningful isolation.
- When `ISO_Index` is high and `COP` is low, relational participation may look limited or weakly reciprocal.
- If `ISO_Index` is high while `SumT_inter` or `Food` also rise, need for closeness may coexist with a tendency toward withdrawal.

## Cautions

- Because it is a ratio, it can be inflated when `R` is low.
- It should not be read as a stand-alone proof of chronic isolation.
- The variable needs context from `COP`, `HumanCont`, `CDI`, and `DEPI`.

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] PER
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] PER

## Aliases

- PER
- personalized answers
- personal frame

## Definition

`PER` shows how much the person tends to justify the response from personal criteria, personal experience, or a private point of view when that style is read at the interpersonal level.
In interpretation, it suggests how much a self-referential frame shapes the person's reading of other people and relational exchange.

## Interpretation

- If `PER` is high, there may be greater tendency to interpret the interpersonal world through personal references rather than shared cues.
- This variable can accompany rigidity, need for self-assertion, or a very private way of validating experience.
- When it appears together with high `Xu%`, interpersonal reading may become even more idiosyncratic.
- A low value only means this bias appears less often; it does not automatically mean the person is open or flexible.

## Cautions

- `PER` is not the same as creativity, and it does not by itself equal narcissism.
- The variable does not measure simple personal opinion; it points to the way the response is supported by a personal frame.
- It should be distinguished from the coding score `PER`, even though the two are related.

## Cautions

- `PER` is not enough by itself to conclude relational egocentricity.
- It should be read with `a:p`, `HumanCont`, `Xu%`, and `H ratio`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `a:p`
- `HumanCont`
- `Xu%`
- `H ratio`
- `COP`

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Pure H
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] Pure H

## Aliases

- Pure H
- pure human
- whole human content

## Definition

`PureH` shows how much human content appears in complete and conventional form, that is, as `H`.
At the interpersonal level, it helps show whether the image of the other tends to be organized as a whole person rather than as a part-object, partial figure, or fantasy human.

## Interpretation

- If `PureH` is relatively high, there is usually more availability to represent people as whole and more integrated figures.
- If `PureH` is low, especially when `HumanCont` is not low, it is worth checking whether human representations are more partial, idealized, or distorted.
- `PureH < 2` often justifies a more careful review of relational style and the quality of human content.
- The variable reflects structural quality of human representation, not interpersonal kindness or sympathy.

## Cautions

- `PureH` is not the same as `HumanCont`; one looks at complete human content and the other looks at total human content.
- A high value does not guarantee mature relatedness if `PHR`, `AG`, or `MOR` are also high.
- A low value does not by itself mean rejection of people.

## Cautions

- To read `PureH` well, it should be compared with `HumanCont`, `GHR`, `PHR`, and `H ratio`.
- Its meaning changes if the protocol contains almost no human responses.

## Variables to Review Together

- `HumanCont`
- `GHR`
- `PHR`
- `H ratio`
- `CDI`

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] SumT

## Aliases

- SumT
- interpersonal SumT
- texture total
- need for closeness

## Definition

`SumT_inter` reads `SumT` from the interpersonal level.
In interpretation, it helps estimate how much need for closeness, contact, and supportive holding appears in relatedness.

## Interpretation

- If `SumT_inter` is high, there may be greater need for emotional proximity and protective contact.
- The value says more about need for closeness than about relational skill.
- If it appears together with `COP`, the search for closeness may be represented inside more reciprocal relationships.
- If it combines with `ISO_Index`, there may be need for closeness alongside distance or isolation.
- With `Food`, the relational need may take on a more dependent or longing quality.

## Cautions

- A high value does not automatically mean good relationships.
- A zero value does not eliminate all need for closeness; it also depends on overall use of shading.
- `SumT` in `Core` should be distinguished from `SumT_inter` in its relational reading.

## Cautions

- This variable needs interpersonal context to become clear.
- It should be read with `Food`, `COP`, `HumanCont`, and `ISO_Index`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `SumT`
- `Food`
- `COP`

- `ISO_Index`

en.title: [Interpretation/Interpersonal] a:p
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Interpersonal] a:p

## Aliases

- a:p
- active:passive
- active-passive ratio

## Definition

`a:p` shows the proportion between active and passive movement when it is read from the interpersonal angle.
In this section, it helps estimate whether the person imagines relatedness from a more active or more receptive position.

## Interpretation

- If the passive pole weighs more heavily, there may be greater expectation of receiving, waiting, or depending on the other person.
- If the active pole dominates, relatedness may be imagined with more initiative, intervention, or self-direction.
- The variable describes relational direction, not total relationship quality.
- Comparing it with `COP`, `AG`, and `SumT_inter` helps distinguish initiative, dependency, and conflict.

## Cautions

- A small difference can be exaggerated if the total amount of movement is low.
- Passive predominance does not automatically equal pathological passivity.
- Active predominance does not automatically equal healthy autonomy; with high `AG`, it can become more controlling or aggressive.

## Cautions

- `a:p` shows only one direction of relational role.
- It should be read with `Ma:Mp`, `COP`, `AG`, `SumT_inter`, and `M`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `a:p`
- `Ma:Mp`
- `COP`
- `AG`
- `SumT_inter`

# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Mediation] Mediation

## Aliases

- mediation
- cognitive mediation

## Definition

`Mediation` gathers the variables used to examine how the person translates the blot into a shareable perception.
This section focuses on adequacy, unusualness, and the degree to which perception departs from shared reality.

## Interpretation

- `XA%`, `WDA%`, `X+%`, and `P` help estimate closeness to more conventional forms of perception.
- `Xu%` shows less common but still possible perceptions.
- `X-%` and `S-%` help estimate how far mediation departs from shared reality.
- This family should be read together with `Processing` and `Ideation`, not by itself.

## Cautions

- A single variable is not enough to summarize all perceptual quality.
- If `R` is low, several ratios become less stable.
- `XA%` and `WDA%` are related but not identical: `WDA%` looks only at more common areas, while `XA%` covers the broader acceptable range.

# [Interpretation/Mediation] P

## Aliases

- P
- Popular

## Definition

`P` indicates how many popular responses appear in the protocol.
In mediation, it helps estimate how closely perception approaches widely shared response patterns.

## Interpretation

- If `P` is low, there may be less overlap with popular readings or greater distance from consensus.
- If `P` is high, there may be greater proximity to common responses or more ease in producing conventional forms.
- Comparing it with `X+%` and `XA%` helps show whether popular consensus matches broader formal adequacy.

## Cautions

- `P` must be coded from the applicable Comprehensive System criteria and interpreted with appropriate cultural context.
- A high value does not automatically mean healthy adaptation, and a low value does not by itself imply pathology.
- It is useful to review on which cards popular responses appear or fail to appear.

[Title] [Interpretation/Mediation] P
[Aliases] P, Popular
[Definition] P indicates how many popular responses appear in the protocol.
In mediation, it helps estimate how closely perception approaches widely shared response patterns.
[Interpretation] If P is low, there may be less overlap with popular readings or greater distance from consensus.

If P is high, there may be greater proximity to common responses or more ease in producing conventional forms.

Comparing it with X+% and XA% helps show whether popular consensus matches broader formal adequacy.
[Cautions] P must be coded from the applicable Comprehensive System criteria and interpreted with appropriate cultural context.

A high value does not automatically mean healthy adaptation, and a low value does not by itself imply pathology.

It is useful to review on which cards popular responses appear or fail to appear.

en.title: [Interpretation/Mediation] S-
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Mediation] S-

## Aliases

- S-
- S-%
- White Space Distortion
- white-space FQ-minus frequency

## Definition

`S-` is the raw frequency of responses that use white space (`S`) and receive minus Form Quality (`FQ-`). The application displays this count, not a percentage, in the Lower Section of the Structural Summary.

## Interpretation

- A nonzero `S-` shows that white-space use and perceptual distortion occurred in the same response.
- Interpret the count in relation to total `R`, total `FQ-`, the number of white-space responses, and the rest of the protocol.
- A separately derived `S-%` is a different variable. Do not read the displayed `S-` count as `S-%` or apply a percentage cutoff directly to it.

## Cautions

- `S-`, total white-space frequency `S`, affective `S_aff`, and the derived ratio `S-%` are distinct variables.
- Do not infer hostility, oppositionality, or psychopathology from the raw count alone.
- If `S-%` is calculated separately, verify its exact denominator and conditions of use.

en.title: [Interpretation/Mediation] WDA%
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Mediation] WDA%

## Aliases

- WDA%
- Form Appropriate Common Areas

## Definition

`WDA%` indicates the proportion of appropriate responses in `W` and `D` areas.
It is used to see how stable mediation remains in relatively common and more easily shared parts of the blot.

## Interpretation

- If `WDA%` is high, perception tends to stay more stable in the more common parts of the material.
- If it drops, even relatively simple areas may show greater perceptual mismatch.
- If `WDA%` stays stronger than `XA%`, difficulty may be concentrated more in complex or less structured responses.

## Cautions

- `WDA%` does not represent the whole protocol; it summarizes only `W` and `D`.
- With few `W` and `D` responses, the ratio can be unstable.
- A low `WDA%` is an important sign, but it does not by itself define clinical severity.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Mediation] XA%
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Mediation] XA%

## Aliases

- XA%
- Form Appropriate Extended

## Definition

`XA%` indicates the overall proportion of responses whose form falls within the extended acceptable range.
Because it includes `FQ+`, `FQo`, and `FQu`, it offers a broad view of perceptual mediation.

## Interpretation

- If `XA%` is high, perception usually remains closer to readings that are still acceptable or shareable.
- If it drops, the probability of distortion, imprecision, or perceptual mismatch increases.
- Comparing it with `WDA%` helps show whether difficulty is broad or more concentrated in complex situations.

## Cautions

- High `XA%` does not mean complete absence of perceptual oddness; `Xu%` can still be important.
- Low `XA%` should be read together with `X-%`, not by itself.
- With few responses, the ratio can fluctuate more.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Mediation] X-%
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Mediation] X-%

## Aliases

- X-%
- Distorted Form

## Definition

`X-%` indicates the proportion of responses with clearly distorted form use.
In mediation, it functions as a central sign of perceptual distance from shared reality.

## Interpretation

- If `X-%` rises, the frequency of perceptions that do not fit the blot well increases.
- If `Xu%` is also high, there may be a mixture of tolerable oddness and genuine distortion.
- If `X-%` is high together with `WSum6` or `PTI`, clinical concern increases.

## Cautions

- `X-%` is not the same as `Xu%`; `Xu%` still reflects an uncommon but possible reading.
- It should be reviewed together with total responses and the broader distribution of `FQ-`.
- A high value is informative, but it does not by itself explain the source of distortion.

en.title: [Interpretation/Mediation] X+%
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Mediation] X+%

## Aliases

- X+%
- Conventional Form

## Definition

`X+%` indicates the proportion of responses whose form is conventionally and clearly shareable.
It summarizes how strongly mediation stays aligned with common readings of the blot.

## Interpretation

- If `X+%` is high, perception usually stays closer to stable and consensual translations.
- If it drops, there may be less reliance on conventional readings and more weight given to unusual or less precise translations.
- Reading it with `P` helps show whether socially shared reference points are still available.

## Cautions

- `X+%` is not the same as `XA%`; `XA%` includes a broader band of adequacy.
- A low `X+%` does not automatically equal severe distortion; `Xu%` and `X-%` also need to be reviewed.
- In short protocols, the ratio can shift with only a few responses.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Mediation] Xu%
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Mediation] Xu%

## Aliases

- Xu%
- Unusual Form

## Definition

`Xu%` indicates the proportion of responses that are formally acceptable but less usual or less conventional.
It marks a style of mediation that can still be sustained, even though it departs further from consensus.

## Interpretation

- If `Xu%` is high, there may be more personal or less conventional translations of the blot.
- If it rises while `X-%` stays low, the oddness may remain tolerable rather than clearly distorted.
- If `Xu%` and `X-%` rise together, perception may become less dependable.

## Cautions

- `Xu%` is not the same as `X-%`; `Xu%` remains acceptable, while `X-%` indicates stronger distortion.
- A high `Xu%` should not be confused immediately with pathology.
- Its meaning changes depending on its relation to `X+%`, `XA%`, `P`, and the rest of the protocol.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Lower Section/Processing] Processing
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Processing] Processing

## Aliases

- processing
- information processing

## Definition

`Processing` gathers the variables that describe how the person scans, organizes, and segments the perceptual field.
This section is usually read through `Zf`, `Zd`, `W:D:Dd`, `W:M`, `PSV`, `DQ+`, and `DQv`.

## Interpretation

- This group helps show how much material is examined, how much complexity is taken in, and how flexibly the field is organized.
- `Zf` and `Zd` help estimate scope and efficiency of scanning.
- `W:D:Dd` and `W:M` show segmentation style and level of organization.
- `PSV`, `DQ+`, and `DQv` add information about repetition, organizational quality, and oversimplification.

## Cautions

- Processing is not the same as mediation; a person can scan widely and still interpret inaccurately.
- Processing is also not the same as ideation; perceptual segmentation and conceptual elaboration are different levels.
- In short protocols, several ratios in this family lose stability.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Processing] DQ+
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Processing] DQ+

## Aliases

- DQ+
- Developmental Quality Plus
- processing DQ+

## Definition

`DQ+` indicates how much integrated, sophisticated organization appears in processing.
In interpretation, it is used as a sign of capacity to structure percepts in a complex and articulated way.

## Interpretation

- If `DQ+` is adequately present, there is usually better capacity to organize complex material in an integrated form.
- When `DQ+` is sustained and `DQv` does not weigh too heavily, processing may look more elaborated and sophisticated.
- The value gains meaning when compared with `Zd`, `PSV`, and the general distribution of developmental quality.

## Cautions

- A high `DQ+` does not automatically mean excellent adaptation.
- If `DQ+` is high but `DQv` is also high, organization may still be uneven.
- `DQ+` should not be confused with `v/+`; they belong to the same coding family but serve different interpretive roles.

## Cautions

- `DQ+` shows a sign of processing sophistication, not a total summary of functioning.
- It should be read with `DQv`, `Zd`, `PSV`, and `W:M`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `DQv`
- `Zd`
- `PSV`
- `W:M`

en.title: [Interpretation/Processing] DQv
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Processing] DQv

## Aliases

- DQv
- Vague Developmental Quality
- processing DQv

## Definition

`DQv` indicates how much vague, simplified, or weakly integrated organization appears in processing.
In interpretation, it works as a sign that organizational quality may drift toward less elaborated forms.

## Interpretation

- If `DQv` rises, processing may become simpler, less integrated, or less precise.
- When `DQv` and `DQv/+` outweigh `DQ+`, processing quality tends to look more fragile.
- The value gains meaning when compared with `Zd`, `PSV`, and the overall developmental quality pattern.

## Cautions

- `DQv` should be read together with `DQv/+`, not treated as the same thing.
- A high value does not by itself explain why organization is reduced.
- It should not be confused with automatic clinical severity.

## Cautions

- `DQv` suggests a weak point in processing, but it does not explain the entire cognitive style by itself.
- It should be read with `DQ+`, `PSV`, `X-%`, and `WSum6`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `DQ+`
- `DQv/+`
- `PSV`
- `X-%`
- `WSum6`

en.title: [Interpretation/Processing] PSV
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Processing] PSV

## Aliases

- PSV
- Perseveration
- processing perseveration

## Definition

`PSV` indicates a tendency to repeat the same approach or remain fixed on a prior pattern during processing.
In interpretation, it functions as a sign of rigidity, difficulty shifting focus, or inefficient attentional control.

## Interpretation

- When `PSV` is present, it is worth checking whether the record shows less flexibility in changing strategy.
- `PSV` combined with other inefficiency indicators strengthens the reading of rigid processing.
- In some records, even a single `PSV` deserves attention because the variable is meant to capture genuine perseveration.

## Cautions

- `PSV` is not the same as normal consistency or stylistic preference.
- The value needs protocol context and the exact form of the coded perseveration.
- It should not be overread without reviewing `Zd`, `DQ`, and other signs of organization.

## Cautions

- `PSV` is a warning sign, not a diagnosis by itself.
- It should be read with `Zd`, `DQ+`, `DQv`, `WSum6`, and `X-%`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `Zd`
- `DQ+`
- `DQv`
- `WSum6`
- `X-%`

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Processing] W:D:Dd

## Aliases

- W:D:Dd
- processing W:D:Dd
- Economy Index

## Definition

`W:D:Dd` shows the proportion of whole responses, common detail responses, and unusual detail responses.
In processing, it is used to see whether the person tends to take in the whole field, focus on common parts, or move toward smaller details.

## Interpretation

- A predominance of `W` suggests more interest in the whole or in broader configurations.
- Greater weight on `D` is usually seen as a more practical and economical style.
- An increase in `Dd` can indicate finer, more particular, or more scattered attention to small details.
- Reading it with `W:M` helps compare perceptual scope with level of organizational ambition.

## Cautions

- No single distribution is pathological by itself.
- The value also depends on total responses and the protocol's broader style.
- A high `Dd` should not automatically be confused with obsessiveness or impairment.

en.title: [Interpretation/Processing] W:M
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Processing] W:M

## Aliases

- W:M
- W_M
- processing W:M
- Aspirational Ratio

## Definition

`W:M` relates the number of `W` responses to the number of `M` responses.
In processing, it is used to estimate whether breadth of approach and ideational resources stay in a workable proportion.

## Interpretation

- If the `W` side dominates too strongly, goals or organizational reach may exceed available ideational resources.
- A more balanced proportion usually suggests a better match between ambitious scanning and actual conceptual resources.
- The value becomes clearer when read together with `AdjD`, `Ma:Mp`, and the general tone of the protocol.

## Cautions

- `W:M` is not a stand-alone index of maturity.
- In records with very few `M` responses, the ratio can be exaggerated.
- Breadth of approach should not be confused with genuine adaptive flexibility.

## Cautions

- `W:M` gives a clue about the relation between breadth and resource, not a total summary of functioning.
- It should be read with `W:D:Dd`, `M`, `Ma:Mp`, `AdjD`, and the rest of the processing cluster.

## Variables to Review Together

- `W:D:Dd`
- `M`
- `Ma:Mp`

- `3r+(2)/R`

en.title: [Interpretation/Processing] Zd
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Processing] Zd

## Aliases

- Zd
- processing Zd
- processing efficiency

## Definition

`Zd` compares the actual level of organizational scanning with the expected level.
It is used to estimate whether processing tends to be balanced, excessive, or insufficient.

## Interpretation

- Values near the expected range suggest a more proportionate scanning and organizing style.
- A strongly positive `Zd` can point to overincorporation or a tendency to take in more than necessary.
- A strongly negative `Zd` can suggest underincorporation or a tendency to move through the field too quickly.
- Reading it with `PSV` helps distinguish inefficiency driven by rigidity from simple perceptual economy.

## Cautions

- A positive `Zd` is not automatically better.
- A negative `Zd` does not by itself imply severe impairment.
- The value needs context from `Zf`, `PSV`, and `W:D:Dd`.

## Cross References

# [Interpretation/Processing] Zf

## Aliases

- Zf
- processing Zf
- Z frequency

## Definition

`Zf` indicates how often the person actively tries to scan and organize the field during processing.
In this section it is used as a frequency measure of organizational effort, not as a measure of efficiency by itself.

## Interpretation

- If `Zf` is high, there are usually more attempts to examine and organize the stimulus.
- If `Zf` is low, there may be less active exploration or less initiative to structure the field.
- Its clinical meaning changes when read together with `Zd`, because frequency and efficiency are not the same.

## Cautions

- A high `Zf` does not automatically mean good processing.
- A low `Zf` can be expected if the protocol is short.
- To interpret the value, the `W:D:Dd` distribution should also be reviewed.

# [Interpretation/Lower Section/Self Perception] Self Perception

## Aliases

- self perception
- self-image
- self-regard

## Definition

`Self Perception` gathers the variables that help read how the person views the self, how much value is assigned to the self, how much self-observation is present, and what tone the self-image takes.
In this cluster, the main review points are `3r+(2)/R`, `Fr+rF`, `SumV`, `FD`, `An+Xy`, `MOR`, and `H ratio`.

## Interpretation

- `3r+(2)/R` helps estimate how much weight the self occupies in the protocol.
- `Fr+rF` helps show whether the self-image needs special shine, enhancement, or confirmation.
- `SumV` and `FD` help distinguish self-criticism, self-observation, and concern about personal limitations.
- `An+Xy`, `MOR`, and `H ratio` help show whether the self-image is experienced as fragile, damaged, partial, or less integrated.

## Cautions

- This cluster does not answer only whether the person "likes" the self or not.
- Self-observation, egocentricity, self-criticism, and bodily vulnerability can rise for different reasons.
- No variable in this family should be read apart from interpersonal and affective context.

## Cautions

- Self-image shifts with affective state, stress, and recent history.
- `Self Perception` should be integrated with `Interpersonal`, `Affect`, and `Core`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `3r+(2)/R`
- `Fr+rF`
- `SumV_self`
- `FD`
- `H_ratio`
