[Aliases] self perception, self-image, self-regard
[Definition] Self Perception gathers the variables that help read how the person views the self, how much value is assigned to the self, how much self-observation is present, and what tone the self-image takes.
In this cluster, the main review points are 3r+(2)/R, Fr+rF, SumV, FD, An+Xy, MOR, and H ratio.
[Interpretation] 3r+(2)/R helps estimate how much weight the self occupies in the protocol.

Fr+rF helps show whether the self-image needs special shine, enhancement, or confirmation.

SumV and FD help distinguish self-criticism, self-observation, and concern about personal limitations.

An+Xy, MOR, and H ratio help show whether the self-image is experienced as fragile, damaged, partial, or less integrated.
[Cautions] This cluster does not answer only whether the person "likes" the self or not.

Self-observation, egocentricity, self-criticism, and bodily vulnerability can rise for different reasons.

No variable in this family should be read apart from interpersonal and affective context.
[Cautions] Self-image shifts with affective state, stress, and recent history.

Self Perception should be integrated with Interpersonal, Affect, and Core.

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] An + Xy
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] An + Xy

## Aliases

- An+Xy
- anatomy plus x-ray
- body concern

## Definition

`An+Xy` combines anatomy content and x-ray content.
In `Self Perception`, it functions as a clue to concern about the body, its functioning, or its vulnerability.

## Interpretation

- If the total is high, there may be greater focus on organs, bodily damage, illness, or physical fragility.
- The variable can appear in somatic concern, body anxiety, or recent health-related stress.
- If it is combined with `MOR_self`, body image may feel more damaged, weak, or alarming.
- Its meaning depends on whether the body appears realistic, feared, or symbolically loaded.

## Cautions

- Medical training, real illness, or recent treatment can raise this variable without special psychopathological meaning.
- `Xy` does not always carry exactly the same meaning as `An` in each response, so the response context still matters.
- A low value does not rule out all body concern.

## Cautions

- The variable points to bodily focus, but does not decide by itself whether that focus is hypochondriacal, traumatic, or situational.
- It should be read together with `MOR_self`, `SumV_self`, and `HVI`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `MOR_self`
- `An`
- `Xy`
- `HVI`
- `SumV_self`

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] FD
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] FD

## Aliases

- FD
- form dimension
- introspection

## Definition

`FD` shows a tendency to step back from experience and to observe the self.
In `Self Perception`, it is used as a clue to introspection and conscious self-observation.

## Interpretation

- If `FD > 0`, there is usually some degree of inward observation of personal functioning.
- That observation can be adaptive, or it can take on criticism, guilt, or discouragement.
- If `FD` appears together with `SumV` or `MOR_self`, introspection may feel heavier or more painful.
- If `FD` appears with a high egocentricity index, much attention may be fixed on the self.

## Cautions

- A high `FD` does not automatically equal good insight.
- `FD = 0` does not prove the total absence of introspection.
- It should be distinguished from the determinant code `FD` and from the content code `Fd`.

## Cautions

- `FD` shows the presence of self-observation, not its quality by itself.
- It should be read together with `SumV`, `MOR_self`, and `3r+(2)/R`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `3r+(2)/R`
- `SumV_self`
- `MOR_self`
- `FD coding`
- `Fd content`

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] Fr + rF
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] Fr + rF

## Aliases

- Fr+rF
- reflection responses
- self-reflection responses

## Definition

`Fr+rF` shows how many reflection responses appear in the protocol.
In `Self Perception`, it helps read whether the self-image needs special shine, confirmation, or an inflated sense of personal importance.

## Interpretation

- If `Fr+rF > 0`, it is worth reviewing increased self-importance or the need to reinforce self-image.
- The variable may relate more to need for reaffirmation than to calm confidence.
- If the egocentricity index is also elevated, self-focus gains even more weight.
- If it appears together with `SumV`, there may be an unstable mix of self-enhancement and self-criticism.

## Cautions

- In adults, reflection responses are not common, so even one instance deserves review.
- Even so, a single reflection does not define the entire personality style.
- Its absence does not prove there is no narcissistic sensitivity or need for validation.

## Cautions

- It should be integrated with `3r+(2)/R`, `SumV`, `FD`, and `MOR`.
- The variable indicates one direction of self-image, not its total stability.

## Variables to Review Together

- `3r+(2)/R`
- `SumV_self`
- `FD`
- `Fr`
- `rF`

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] H Ratio
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] H Ratio

## Aliases

- H ratio
- H:(H)+Hd+(Hd)
- human image ratio

## Definition

`H_ratio` compares whole human content with partial or imagined human content.
In `Self Perception`, it helps show whether the image of self and others rests more on whole, realistic human figures or on partial, imagined, or less integrated figures.

## Interpretation

- If `H` carries more weight, human representation may rest on a more complete and better integrated base.
- If `(H)`, `Hd`, or `(Hd)` dominate, the human image may feel more partial, idealized, or fragmented.
- Read together with `HumanCont` and `PureH`, it helps estimate the quality of general human representation.
- If `PHR` is high and `H_ratio` is unfavorable, human representations may look more tense or damaged.

## Cautions

- If total human content is very low, the ratio becomes less stable.
- `Hx` is not formally part of the ratio, although it still matters as context.
- It should be read cautiously in artistic, highly symbolic, or culture-shaped responses.

## Cautions

- `H_ratio` does not define self-esteem or mood by itself.
- It should be read together with `MOR_self`, `HumanCont`, `GHR`, and `PHR`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `HumanCont`
- `PureH`
- `GHR`
- `PHR`
- `MOR_self`

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] MOR
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] MOR

## Aliases

- MOR
- morbid self-image
- damaged self-image

## Definition

`MOR` in `Self Perception` shows how much the self-image is experienced as damaged, defective, worn down, or without value.
Where `MOR` in `Ideation` describes a general tone of thinking, the focus here is how much of that tone falls on the representation of the self.

## Interpretation

- If the value is high, the person may feel marked by flaw, damage, or personal defect.
- If it is combined with `SumV_self`, negative self-image may be accompanied by intense self-criticism.
- If `An_Xy` is also high, the body image may feel more fragile, deteriorated, or threatening.
- If `MOR` is high in both ideation and self-perception, the negative tone may be broad and also deeply personal.

## Cautions

- High `MOR_self` does not automatically equal clinical depression.
- Real illness, physical trauma, or a period of loss can increase damaged self-image reactively.
- A zero value does not guarantee a healthy or stable self-image.

## Cautions

- `MOR_self` shows the negative tone of self-image, but does not explain by itself how that experience is defended or regulated.
- It should be read together with `SumV_self`, `FD`, `Fr+rF`, and `DEPI`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `ideation MOR`
- `SumV_self`
- `An_Xy`
- `DEPI`
- `FD`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Self Perception] Self Perception](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception)

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] SumV
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] SumV

## Aliases

- SumV
- self perception SumV
- vista total
- self-criticism and self-observation

## Definition

`SumV` in `Self Perception` helps read how much critical self-observation, painful self-awareness, or review of personal limitations enters the self-image.
In `Core`, it also relates to overall burden, but here the emphasis is on self-evaluation.

## Interpretation

- If `SumV` is high, self-observation may lean toward guilt, shame, defect, or a sense of insufficiency.
- The variable can show that the person views the self harshly or with marked sensitivity to personal flaws.
- If `FD` also rises, self-observation may become more conscious and sustained.
- If it appears with `MOR_self`, self-image may feel more damaged or impoverished.

## Cautions

- `SumV > 0` does not by itself prove disorder or depression.
- The variable can rise reactively during loss, frustration, or stress.
- A value of zero does not mean total absence of self-criticism.

## Cautions

- `SumV` should be read with `FD`, `Fr+rF`, `MOR_self`, and `AdjD`.
- Its meaning changes if the record shows very little general introspection.

## Variables to Review Together

- `core SumV`
- `FD`
- `Fr+rF`
- `MOR_self`
- `AdjD`

[Interpretation] If SumV is high, self-observation may lean toward guilt, shame, defect, or a sense of insufficiency.

The variable can show that the person views the self harshly or with marked sensitivity to personal flaws.

If FD also rises, self-observation may become more conscious and sustained.

If it appears with MOR\_self, self-image may feel more damaged or impoverished.
[Cautions] SumV > 0 does not by itself prove disorder or depression.

The variable can rise reactively during loss, frustration, or stress.

A value of zero does not mean total absence of self-criticism.
[Cautions] SumV should be read with FD, Fr+rF, MOR\_self, and AdjD.

Its meaning changes if the record shows very little general introspection.

en.title: [Interpretation/Self Perception] Egocentricity Index
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Self Perception] Egocentricity Index

## Aliases

- 3r+(2)/R
- Egocentricity Index
- egocentricity ratio

## Definition

`3r+(2)/R` is an egocentricity index calculated as `[3 x (Fr + rF) + Sum(2)] / R`. Each reflection determinant is therefore weighted as three pair responses; the multiplier is not two despite the `(2)` pair notation in the label.
In interpretation, it helps estimate how much weight the self, personal value, or personal importance occupies in the perceptual field.

## Interpretation

- If the index is high, there may be greater self-focus, need for self-confirmation, or sensitivity to personal value.
- If it is very high, not only self-interest but also the need to validate or protect self-esteem may increase.
- If it is low, there may be less self-assertion, less investment in personal importance, or diminished self-valuation.
- The index reflects self-concern, not healthy self-esteem by itself.

## Cautions

- In adults, values below `.33` or above `.44` often deserve more careful review, but the index does not decide by itself.
- If `R` is low, the ratio can look more extreme than it really is.
- A high value does not automatically equal clinical narcissism.

## Cautions

- This index should be read with `Fr+rF`, `FD`, `SumV`, `MOR`, and `H ratio`.
- Its meaning changes if there are very few pair responses or very few total responses.

## Variables to Review Together

- `Fr+rF`
- `FD`
- `H_ratio`
- `R`
- `pair`

en.title: [Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices

## Aliases

- special indices
- constellations
- composite indices

## Definition

`Special Indices` gathers composite constellations built from multiple protocol variables.
Each index does not replace clinical interpretation; instead it works as an actuarial screen that helps decide which areas need priority review.

## Interpretation

- `PTI` points to problems in thinking and mediation.
- `DEPI` organizes an alert around depressive features.
- `CDI` summarizes vulnerability in coping resources and interpersonal effectiveness.
- `SCON` is a high-stakes risk alert. `HVI` and `OBS` organize vigilance- and precision-related variable patterns, but their empirical support is weak or insufficient and they should remain low-confidence hypotheses.

## Cautions

- No special index should be treated as an automatic diagnosis.
- Evidence strength differs by index; meeting an operational cutoff is not the same as establishing its proposed clinical meaning.
- Constellations can produce false positives or miss individual cases.
- It is always necessary to return to the base variables that feed the index.

## Cautions

- These indices are screening shortcuts, not substitutes for domain-based reading.
- They should be reconsidered in light of `Ideation`, `Affect`, `Interpersonal`, and `Self Perception`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `PTI`
- `DEPI`
- `CDI`
- `SCON`
- `HVI`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation] result-interpretation](ref://result-interpretation)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] PTI](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/PTI)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] DEPI](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/DEPI)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] CDI](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/CDI)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Suicide Constellation](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/SCON)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Hypervigilance Index](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/HVI)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Obsessive Style Index](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/OBS)
- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Ideation] Ideation](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation)
- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Affect] Affect](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/affect)
- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Interpersonal] Interpersonal](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal)

## Evidence Strength

- Evidence tier: `mixed`
- The special indices do not have interchangeable empirical support. PTI and S-CON are relatively well supported, DEPI and CDI have limited support, and support for HVI and OBS is weak or insufficient.
- Use every index as a screening hypothesis and cross-check it against component variables, interview data, observed behavior, and history.

en.title: [Interpretation/Special Indices] CDI
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Special Indices] CDI

## Aliases

- CDI
- Coping Deficit Index
- coping deficit index

## Definition

`CDI` combines variables related to coping resources and interpersonal effectiveness.
A positive result calls for closer assessment but does not itself establish that the person is poorly equipped to handle demand or relational pressure.

## Interpretation

- If `CDI` is positive, coping resources, dependency, interpersonal inefficiency, and low tolerance for demand should be reviewed.
- The index usually carries more weight when it appears with `Food`, `SumT_inter`, `ISO_Index`, `PureH`, and `EA`.
- Review observed coping, support needs, and flexibility under stress directly rather than inferring them from the index.
- If `DEPI` is also positive, vulnerability may be mixed with depressive tone.

## Cautions

- `CDI` is not a depression index.
- It should not be treated as proof of fixed immaturity or a permanent trait.
- Empirical support is limited, so current context and component variables carry more weight than the positive/negative label.
- Age, social support, and current demands can strongly change its meaning.

## Cautions

- The index points to risk of insufficient resources, but not to its cause by itself.
- It is important to return to `Food`, `SumT_inter`, `ISO_Index`, `PureH`, and `EA`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `Food`
- `SumT_inter`
- `ISO_Index`
- `PureH`
- `EA`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices)
- [[Interpretation/Interpersonal] Food](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/Food)
- [[Interpretation/Interpersonal] SumT](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/SumT_inter)
- [[Interpretation/Interpersonal] Isolation Index](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/ISO_Index)
- [[Interpretation/Interpersonal] Pure H](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/PureH)
- [[Interpretation/Core] EA](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/EA)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] DEPI](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/DEPI)

## Evidence Strength

- Evidence tier: `limited`
- Empirical associations with coping and interpersonal vulnerability are limited. A positive result does not establish helplessness, immaturity, dependency, or a fixed trait.
- Review current stress, observed coping behavior, social support, developmental and cultural context, and the component variables.

en.title: [Interpretation/Special Indices] DEPI
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Special Indices] DEPI

## Aliases

- DEPI
- Depression Index
- depression index

## Definition

`DEPI` is a composite index that summarizes how many signs in the protocol point toward depressive features.
It integrates variables from affect, burden, negative self-image, and emotional withdrawal.

## Interpretation

- If `DEPI` is positive, assess depressive symptoms more closely without assuming that discouragement, hopelessness, guilt, or loss of energy is present from the index alone.
- The index gains meaning when it appears together with `SumV`, `SumY`, `MOR_self`, and altered `Afr`.
- Its empirical support is limited, so it sets an assessment priority rather than establishing a probable depressive pattern or episode.
- If `CDI` is also positive, vulnerability may be mixed with a stronger sense of helplessness.

## Cautions

- A positive `DEPI` is not automatically a formal diagnosis.
- A negative `DEPI` does not exclude depression.
- Life context, grief, and recent stress can influence the constellation.

## Cautions

- The base variables should be reviewed before fixing a clinical conclusion.
- It should be integrated with `Affect`, `SumV`, `SumY`, `MOR_self`, and `CDI`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `SumV`
- `SumY`
- `MOR_self`
- `Afr`
- `CDI`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices)
- [[Interpretation/Lower Section/Affect] Affect](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/affect)
- [[Interpretation/Core] SumV](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/SumV)
- [[Interpretation/Core] SumY](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/SumY)
- [[Interpretation/Self Perception] MOR](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception/MOR_self)
- [[Interpretation/Affect] Afr](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/affect/Afr)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] CDI](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/CDI)

## Evidence Strength

- Evidence tier: `limited`
- Empirical support for depression-related constructs is limited. A positive result calls for further assessment; it is not evidence of particular symptoms or a diagnosis.
- Separately assess current mood, anhedonia, sleep and appetite, guilt, suicidal ideation, duration, and functional impairment, and do not use a negative result to rule out depression.

en.title: [Interpretation/Special Indices] Hypervigilance Index
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Special Indices] Hypervigilance Index

## Aliases

- HVI
- Hypervigilance Index
- hypervigilance index

## Definition

`HVI` is a yes/no combination of variables proposed to reflect defensive alertness and interpersonal distance.
Empirical support for interpreting it as hypervigilance or distrust is weak and inconsistent, so a positive result remains a low-confidence hypothesis.

## Interpretation

- If `HVI` is positive, first determine whether actual danger, trauma history, cultural guardedness, or independently observed vigilance supports the hypothesis.
- The pattern is usually read more as defensive disposition than as an automatic paranoid diagnosis.
- The constellation gains meaning when it appears with `SumT_inter`, `Zf`, `Zd`, `S_aff`, `H_ratio`, and `HumanCont`.
- Real danger or recent threat experiences can also affect the pattern.

## Cautions

- The yes/no decision does not establish vigilance when positive, and its absence does not rule out elevated vigilance.
- Cultural and situational factors can influence reserve, distance, and guardedness.
- The primary `T = 0` rule and the secondary conditions need to be read together.

## Cautions

- `HVI` shows a pattern of alertness and defense, not its cause by itself.
- It should be reviewed together with `S`, `Zf`, `Zd`, `H_ratio`, and interpersonal variables.

## Variables to Review Together

- `SumT_inter`
- `Zf_proc`
- `Zd_proc`
- `S_aff`
- `H_ratio`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices)
- [[Interpretation/Interpersonal] SumT](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/SumT_inter)
- [[Interpretation/Processing] Zf](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/processing/Zf_proc)
- [[Interpretation/Processing] Zd](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/processing/Zd_proc)
- [[Interpretation/Affect] S](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/affect/S_aff)
- [[Interpretation/Self Perception] H Ratio](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception/H_ratio)
- [[Interpretation/Interpersonal] Human Content](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/HumanCont)

## Evidence Strength

- Evidence tier: `weak-inconsistent`
- Empirical support for interpreting HVI as hypervigilance or distrust is weak and inconsistent.
- Keep a positive result as a low-confidence organizing hypothesis unless actual danger, trauma history, cultural guardedness, and independently observed vigilance support it.

# [Interpretation/Special Indices] Obsessive Style Index

## Aliases

- OBS
- Obsessive Style Index
- obsessive style index

## Definition

`OBS` is a yes/no combination of variables related to precision, detail focus, and organization.
Construct-validity evidence is insufficient for using it to infer obsessive personality features or impairment.

## Interpretation

- A positive result first means that the operational variable combination was met; verify overcontrol, perfectionism, and rigidity independently in interview and behavior.
- That style can improve order and precision, but it can also make processing more rigid.
- The constellation gains weight when `Zf`, `Zd`, `Dd`, `P`, and `FQ+` cluster together.
- The index points to stylistic direction, not to obsessive-compulsive disorder by itself.

## Cautions

- `OBS` is yes/no, does not measure degree, and does not by itself establish the proposed style.
- It should not be confused with a diagnosis of OCD.
- Technical or cultural contexts that reward control can increase this style without pathology.

## Cautions

- To understand the style, the base variables must be reviewed.
- It should be read together with `Zf`, `Zd`, `Dd`, `P`, and `FQ+`.

## Variables to Review Together

- `Zf_proc`
- `Zd_proc`
- `Dd`
- `P`
- `FQ+`

en.title: [Interpretation/Special Indices] PTI
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Special Indices] PTI

## Aliases

- PTI
- Perceptual-Thinking Index
- perceptual-thinking index

## Definition

`PTI` is a composite index that groups signs of perceptual and thinking disorganization.
Its function is to alert the reader to review possible distortion of reality, ideational slippage, or loss of perceptual precision.

## Interpretation

- If `PTI` is positive, mediation and ideation should be reviewed first.
- The index usually becomes more meaningful when problems converge in `WSum6`, `Lv2`, `M-`, `X-%`, and `XA%`.
- Its interpretation points to possible thought disturbance, not an automatic diagnosis.
- The index gains weight when several different parts of the protocol point in the same direction.

## Cautions

- A positive `PTI` does not by itself mean psychosis.
- A negative `PTI` does not remove all possibility of disturbed thinking.
- Extreme stress, intoxication, situational disorganization, or very low response volume can complicate the reading.

## Cautions

- `PTI` is an actuarial signal and requires returning to the base variables.
- `WSum6`, `Lv2`, `M-`, `X-%`, and `XA%` should be reviewed before drawing strong conclusions.

## Variables to Review Together

- `WSum6`
- `Lv2`
- `M_minus`
- `X_minus_percent`
- `XA_percent`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices)
- [[Interpretation/Ideation] WSum6](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation/WSum6)
- [[Interpretation/Ideation] Lv2](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation/Lv2)
- [[Interpretation/Ideation] M-](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/ideation/M_minus)
- [[Interpretation/Mediation] X-%](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/mediation/X_minus_percent)
- [[Interpretation/Mediation] XA%](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/mediation/XA_percent)

## Evidence Strength

- Evidence tier: `supported`
- Empirical support is relatively strong among the special indices, but PTI cannot independently diagnose a thought disorder or psychotic disorder.
- Review the actual WSum6, Lv2, M-, X-%, and XA% pattern and consider acute stress, intoxication, developmental factors, and short records instead of relying on the positive/negative label alone.

en.title: [Interpretation/Special Indices] Suicide Constellation
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Special Indices] Suicide Constellation

## Aliases

- S-CON
- Suicide Constellation
- suicide constellation

## Definition

`S-CON` is an actuarial constellation that groups signs associated with greater suicide risk.
It does not replace immediate clinical assessment, but indicates when the issue needs high priority attention.

## Interpretation

- Apply the S-CON threshold and interpretation only to examinees age 15 or older. Its usefulness has not been demonstrated for age 14 or younger, so do not treat a computed score as a positive or negative conclusion in that group.
- The result is positive when at least 8 of these 12 criteria are met: `FV+VF+V+FD > 2`, Color-Shading blends `> 0`, `3r+(2)/R < .31` or `> .44`, `MOR > 3`, `Zd < -3.5` or `> +3.5`, `es > EA`, `CF+C > FC`, `X+% < .70`, `S > 3`, `P < 3` or `> 8`, `Pure H < 2`, and `R < 17`.
- If `S-CON` reaches threshold, directly assess suicidal ideation, intent, plan, access to means, prior attempts, recent changes, and protective factors immediately.
- The constellation integrates signs of stress, self-criticism, emotional pain, and reduced control.
- Its weight increases when it appears with low `D`, low `AdjD`, `SumV`, `SumY`, `MOR_self`, and `DEPI`.
- It functions as a screening alert, not a final conclusion.

## Cautions

- A high value does not by itself mean imminent suicidal action.
- A low value does not remove all risk.
- Because suicide has a low base rate, positive results can also be false positives; neither result replaces direct risk assessment.
- Short or highly defensive records can produce false negatives.

## Cautions

- `S-CON` must be checked against interview data, recent history, and direct clinical judgment.
- The reader should return to the variables that compose the constellation.

## Variables to Review Together

- `D`
- `AdjD`
- `SumV`
- `SumY`
- `MOR_self`

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] Special Indices](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices)
- [[Interpretation/Core] D](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/D)
- [[Interpretation/Core] AdjD](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/AdjD)
- [[Interpretation/Core] SumV](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/SumV)
- [[Interpretation/Core] SumY](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/core/SumY)
- [[Interpretation/Self Perception] SumV](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception/SumV_self)
- [[Interpretation/Self Perception] MOR](ref://result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception/MOR_self)
- [[Interpretation/Special Indices] DEPI](ref://result-interpretation/special-indices/DEPI)

## Evidence Strength

- Evidence tier: `supported-high-stakes`
- Its association with suicide-related risk is relatively strong, but the low base rate of suicide permits false positives and a negative result cannot rule out risk.
- Regardless of the score, directly assess current ideation, intent, plan, access to means, prior attempts, recent changes, and protective factors, and prioritize appropriate safety action.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Upper Section] Upper Section

## Aliases

- upper-section
- upper section
- upper section of structural summary

## Definition

`Upper Section` is the part of the structural summary where `Zf`, `ZSum`, `ZEst`, `Zd`, `W`, `D`, `Dd`, `S`, and the `DQ` distribution are reviewed first.
It works as an initial screen for how the person organizes the stimulus field, where attention is placed, and how well responses are generally structured.

## Interpretation

- The `Z` family helps estimate frequency, energy, and efficiency of organizational effort.
- `W`, `D`, `Dd`, and `S` show whether attention is directed toward wholes, common details, unusual details, or white space.
- The `DQ` distribution summarizes the general level of formal integration or organization in the responses.
- This block usually connects next with `processing` and `mediation`.

## Cautions

- `Zf` or `ZSum` alone are not enough; `Zd` usually matters as well.
- A high `W` count does not automatically mean efficient broad scanning.
- A high `Dd` or `S` count should not be read as pathology by itself.
- Low `DQ+` can also appear in brief or highly defensive protocols.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] D

## Aliases

- D
- common detail
- ordinary detail responses

## Definition

`D` is the frequency of responses given to common details of the blot.
In interpretation it serves as a basic indicator of attention to practical, usual, and relatively shared units.

## Interpretation

- A proportionate `D` is often compatible with focus on concrete and manageable elements.
- A prominent `D` may suggest preference for common, workable parts of the stimulus.
- If `D` clearly dominates `W` and `Dd`, the style may be more practical than exploratory.

## Cautions

- High `D` does not by itself prove adaptation or better reality testing.
- If `D` is high but `P` is low or `Xu%` is high, the apparent conventionality may not hold.
- Low `D` should be read together with `W` and `Dd`, not by itself.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] Dd

## Aliases

- Dd
- unusual detail
- rare detail responses

## Definition

`Dd` is the frequency of responses given to unusual or infrequently used details.
In interpretation it indicates how much attention shifts toward less shared or less obvious parts of the stimulus.

## Interpretation

- Some `Dd` may suggest exploratory breadth or sensitivity to less salient detail.
- High `Dd` may accompany idiosyncratic focus, unconventional interest, or very peripheral scanning.
- Very low `Dd` may reflect staying with more typical and expected units.

## Cautions

- High `Dd` does not automatically equal creativity.
- If `Dd` rises with low `P` and high `Xu%`, the reading leans more toward unconventional perception.
- If `Dd` rises with very positive `Zd`, overinspection may be more likely than creativity.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] S

## Aliases

- S
- space responses
- white space responses

## Definition

`S` is the frequency of responses that use white space as the main location.
Within `Upper Section` it is read as a clue about reversed focus, opposition, or unconventional exploration of the field.

## Interpretation

- Some `S` may accompany independent focus or critical exploration of the stimulus.
- High `S` may suggest opposition, nonconformity, or a tendency to look where others do not.
- Low `S` simply indicates that white space was not an important resource in the protocol.

## Cautions

- High `S` should not be reduced immediately to rebellion.
- If `S` rises with `S-%`, `X-%`, `AG`, or `PER`, the meaning may lean toward greater conflict or inefficiency.
- If it appears with good mediation and good formal control, it may also reflect flexibility or originality.

[Title] [Interpretation/Upper Section] S
[Aliases] S, space responses, white space responses
[Definition] S is the frequency of responses that use white space as the main location.
Within Upper Section it is read as a clue about reversed focus, opposition, or unconventional exploration of the field.
[Interpretation] Some S may accompany independent focus or critical exploration of the stimulus.

Low S simply indicates that white space was not an important resource in the protocol.
[Cautions] High S should not be reduced immediately to rebellion.

If S rises with S-%, X-%, AG, or PER, the meaning may lean toward greater conflict or inefficiency.

If it appears with good mediation and good formal control, it may also reflect flexibility or originality.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] W

## Aliases

- W
- whole responses
- whole-card responses

## Definition

`W` is the frequency of responses given to the whole blot.
In interpretation it shows how much the person tries to take in the stimulus field as a whole and whether that broad focus seems useful or not.

## Interpretation

- An adequate `W` may go with the ability to take in broader context.
- A high `W` may suggest a tendency to begin with the whole or to work in larger units.
- A low `W` may suggest greater emphasis on details than on the total configuration.

## Cautions

- High `W` does not automatically mean efficient synthesis; `DQ`, `FQ`, `W:M`, and `Zd` still matter.
- Low `W` does not by itself equal narrowness; it may coexist with a practical, detail-oriented style.
- If `W` is high while `Dd` is also high, broad scanning may coexist with dispersion.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] ZEst

## Aliases

- ZEst
- estimated Z sum
- expected Z sum

## Definition

`ZEst` is the estimated `ZSum` expected from the observed value of `Zf`.
It functions as a baseline for calculating `Zd` more than as an independent clinical variable.

## Interpretation

- `ZEst` works as a reference value.
- It allows comparison between actual organization (`ZSum`) and what would be expected.
- Interpretive emphasis usually falls on `Zd`, not on `ZEst` alone.

## Cautions

- A high `ZEst` often simply reflects that `Zf` is also high.
- It is better to avoid phrases like "high ZEst" or "low ZEst" unless its comparative role is explained.

en.title: [Interpretation/Upper Section] ZSum
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Upper Section] ZSum

## Aliases

- ZSum
- weighted Z sum
- total Z score

## Definition

`ZSum` is the sum of the weights assigned to responses that receive a `Z` score.
It reflects not only how often organization was attempted, but also how much total organizational effort was invested.

## Interpretation

- `ZSum` summarizes total organizational energy.
- A high value may accompany a stronger tendency to connect relations within the field.
- A low value may go with simpler or less frequent organizational attempts.
- Its main interpretive value depends on comparison with `ZEst`, which leads to `Zd`.

## Cautions

- A high `ZSum` may be quite reasonable if `Zf` is also high.
- A low `ZSum` should not automatically be read as a processing deficit.
- The key question is whether the difference from `ZEst` stays within an efficient range.

## Cross References

en.title: [Interpretation/Upper Section] Zd
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Upper Section] Zd

## Aliases

- Zd
- Z difference
- difference between ZSum and ZEst

## Definition

`Zd` is the difference between actual organization (`ZSum`) and expected organization (`ZEst`).
It is the most direct indicator of organizational efficiency within the `Z` family.

## Interpretation

- A `Zd` near zero often suggests a reasonable balance between organizational frequency and load.
- A clearly positive `Zd` may point to overincorporation, excessive checking, or too much elaboration of the field.
- A clearly negative `Zd` may suggest underincorporation, rushing, or insufficient inspection of the stimulus.

## Cautions

- A positive value should not automatically be confused with adaptive thoroughness.
- A negative value should not automatically be translated into impairment.
- Meaning improves when it is reviewed together with `Lambda`, `R`, `Zf`, and `ZSum`.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Interpretation/Upper Section] Zf

## Aliases

- Zf
- Z frequency
- frequency of Z responses

## Definition

`Zf` is the frequency of responses that receive a `Z` score.
It shows how often the person attempts to organize relationships among parts of the stimulus field.

## Interpretation

- `Zf` first reflects how often organizational effort appears.
- An adequate `Zf` is usually compatible with exploration that is neither overly shallow nor excessively tied up in the field.
- A high `Zf` may suggest a tendency to organize and check relations frequently.
- A low `Zf` may accompany simple responses or fewer efforts at structuring.

## Cautions

- `Zf` should be reviewed together with `ZSum` and `Zd`.
- A high `Zf` does not by itself mean good efficiency.
- A low `Zf` does not automatically imply impairment; short protocols and defensiveness can also lower it.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] DQo

## Aliases

- DQo
- ordinary developmental quality
- number of DQo responses

## Definition

`DQo` is the frequency of responses with ordinary developmental quality.
It usually functions as the baseline for the protocol's usual level of organization.

## Interpretation

- In many protocols, `DQo` forms the central part of the `DQ` distribution.
- A proportionate `DQo` may reflect a common, stable level of organization.
- A very strong predominance of `DQo` may indicate a fairly conventional and not very complex style.

## Cautions

- High `DQo` is not necessarily a weakness.
- Its meaning changes with the relation to `DQ+`, `DQv/+`, and `DQv`.
- If `DQo` dominates and `DQ+` is almost absent, integrative complexity may be limited.

## Cross References

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] DQ+

## Aliases

- DQ+
- synthesized responses
- number of DQ+ responses

## Definition

`DQ+` is the frequency of responses with well-integrated developmental quality.
In interpretation it indicates how often complex and well-articulated organization appears in the protocol.

## Interpretation

- The presence of `DQ+` suggests capacity to integrate parts of the stimulus into more complex configurations.
- Relatively high `DQ+` may reflect greater organizational complexity available within the protocol.
- Low `DQ+` may indicate predominance of simpler responses or fewer attempts at integration.

## Cautions

- High `DQ+` should not automatically be interpreted as superior cognitive ability.
- If `DQ+` is high but `FQ` or `Zd` are weak, the complexity may not be efficient.
- Low `DQ+` can also appear in brief or highly defensive protocols.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] DQv

## Aliases

- DQv
- vague responses
- number of vague responses

## Definition

`DQv` is the frequency of responses with vague or weakly structured organization.
It helps estimate how often the protocol produces responses that are poorly defined at the level of integration.

## Interpretation

- High `DQv` may suggest loose organization, poor differentiation, or weakly elaborated responses.
- If it appears repeatedly across the protocol, instability in organizational level should be considered.
- Low `DQv` indicates that vagueness is not a dominant feature of the record.

## Cautions

- `DQv` should be distinguished from `DQv/+`.
- High `DQv` in a very brief protocol should not be overread.
- Interpretation improves when `FQ`, `Lambda`, and `DQ_v_proc` are reviewed with it.

# [Interpretation/Upper Section] DQv/+

## Aliases

- DQv/+
- vague synthesized responses
- number of DQv/+ responses

## Definition

`DQv/+` is the frequency of responses that show an attempt at synthesis, but with a vague organizational base.
It is a mixed signal: there is integrative effort, but the structural support is not fully firm.

## Interpretation

- `DQv/+` shows more organizational effort than `DQv`.
- At the same time, the perceptual base remains less clear than in `DQ+`.
- A small amount may appear as a by-product of complex attempts that are not fully stabilized.

## Cautions

- If `DQv/+` rises together with `DQv`, the pattern leans more toward imprecise organization than efficient integration.
- If `DQv/+` appears with good formal quality and without excessive vagueness, it may reflect an effort toward complexity rather than disorganization.
- It should not be confused with `DQ+`.

## Cross References

- [[Interpretation/Upper Section] Upper Section](ref://result-interpretation/upper-section)

[Title] [Interpretation/Upper Section] DQv/+
[Aliases] DQv/+, vague synthesized responses, number of DQv/+ responses
[Definition] DQv/+ is the frequency of responses that show an attempt at synthesis, but with a vague organizational base.
It is a mixed signal: there is integrative effort, but the structural support is not fully firm.
[Interpretation] DQv/+ shows more organizational effort than DQv.

At the same time, the perceptual base remains less clear than in DQ+.

A small amount may appear as a by-product of complex attempts that are not fully stabilized.
[Cautions] If DQv/+ rises together with DQv, the pattern leans more toward imprecise organization than efficient integration.

If DQv/+ appears with good formal quality and without excessive vagueness, it may reflect an effort toward complexity rather than disorganization.

It should not be confused with DQ+.

# [Coding] scoring-input

## Aliases

- scoring-input
- scoring input
- coding input
- coding

## Definition

`scoring-input` names the full phase in which each response is converted into Comprehensive System codes.
This page does not interpret structural-summary variables; it maps the coding families used before interpretation begins.

## Conditions

- Coding is done response by response, in the actual order of the protocol.
- For each response, it is usually safest to check location, DQ, determinants, FQ, content, and supplementary codes in a consistent sequence.
- When applicable, `Pair`, `Popular`, `Z`, `GHR/PHR`, and `Special Scores` are added as well.
- Coding decisions should come from the response plus the relevant inquiry, not from a later global impression of the person.
- The goal of this phase is to record each response in symbols accurately enough to support the structural summary.

## Cautions

- Coding is not the same task as interpretation.
- In this phase, accurate description of the response matters more than broad clinical meaning.
- A card or context may guide attention, but the final code still depends on the concrete features of the response.
- The same sign can mean different things in different contexts.
- For example, `Card V` is not the determinant `V`.
- In the same way, `DQ +` is not `FQ +`.

# [Coding/Cards] Card

## Aliases

- Card
- cards
- plates
- inkblot cards

## Definition

`Card` is the guide page for the 10 cards in the Comprehensive System.  
This family does not interpret the global symbolic meaning of each card; it works as a coding aid for remembering where certain response patterns tend to appear more easily.

## Conditions

- Card pages help review common responses, `Popular` possibilities, location tendencies, and determinants that often appear more easily on each plate.
- Coding is always decided from the examinee's actual response, not from the card alone.
- The same response can change code if the real description does not confirm what that card often facilitates.
- The route skeleton is shared across locales, but the body and cross-references may vary by language and culture.

## Cautions

- Card pages are not symbolic interpretation pages for the blots.
- They should be read as coding support, not as automatic rules.
- A card number can resemble letters used in other codes, so the context must always stay explicit.
- For example, `Card V` is not the same thing as determinant `V`.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Coding/Cards] I

## Aliases

- Card I
- card I
- card 1
- plate I

## Definition

`Card I` is the first plate in the protocol.  
This page summarizes the kinds of responses that often appear when coding begins; it is not a symbolic interpretation of the card.

## Conditions

- Global `W` responses are common on `Card I`.
- Simple form responses such as bat, butterfly, or other broad animal figures often appear.
- When the response uses the whole blot with clear organization, review `F`, `FQ`, and `Popular`.
- If the person uses only a small part of the blot, the card by itself does not justify `Popular`.

## Cautions

- Do not code `Popular` just because the response sounds familiar; it has to meet the formal standard for that card.
- `Card I` and `Card V` share bat or butterfly-type responses, but they are not treated as the same plate.
- Mentioning dark color verbally is not enough to add another determinant.

en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Coding/Cards] II

## Aliases

- Card II
- card II
- card 2
- plate II

## Definition

`Card II` introduces striking red areas early in the protocol.  
This page summarizes how that chromatic presence may influence coding without turning the card into an automatic rule.

## Conditions

- If the red actually participates in the response, review `FC`, `CF`, or `C`.
- If color is mentioned only as location and not as a quality used to build the perception, do not add a chromatic determinant.
- The organization among dark, light, and red areas can make it useful to review `Z`.
- Some responses look like humans or animals in interaction, but movement still has to be confirmed separately.

## Cautions

- Seeing red is not enough by itself to assign a color code.
- The card may facilitate several perceptual parts, so confirm whether the answer is one response or several separate responses.
- The simple presence of two figures does not by itself create `COP` or `AG`.

# [Coding/Cards] III

## Aliases

- Card III
- card III
- card 3
- plate III

## Definition

`Card III` often facilitates human responses and scenes of interaction.  
This page functions as a coding reminder for human content, movement, and relational quality.

## Conditions

- Responses with two people, two human figures, or figures in relation are common.
- If human movement is clear, review `M`.
- If the response shows cooperation or aggression between moving figures, review `COP` and `AG`.
- Because human content often appears here, it is also useful to review `H` and the `GHR / PHR` decision.

## Cautions

- The mere presence of two figures is not enough for `COP` or `AG`.
- A response that looks social does not automatically mean human movement.
- If the scene is organized as two separate objects without a defined action, do not add relational codes just by intuition.

# [Coding/Cards] IV

## Aliases

- Card IV
- card IV
- card 4
- plate IV

## Definition

`Card IV` often facilitates global responses and comments tied to form, texture, or visual weight.  
This page summarizes what is useful to review when coding those responses.

## Conditions

- `W` responses are common on `Card IV`.
- If the subject describes texture or tactile quality, review `T` or `TF` depending on the role of form.
- If the response remains mainly formal, review `F` and `FQ`.
- The fact that the card looks heavy or shaded does not by itself add a shading determinant.

## Cautions

- Verbal descriptions of roughness or weight are not enough unless they actually shape the coded perception.
- This page does not interpret the symbolism of the card; it only flags coding focal points.
- `Card IV` and determinant `V` are different things and should not be confused.

# [Coding/Cards] IX

## Aliases

- Card IX
- card IX
- card 9
- plate IX

## Definition

`Card IX` often requires more organization in order to maintain good form.  
This page summarizes what to watch in human content, movement, and formal quality.

## Conditions

- Some responses on this card approach human or humanoid figures, so it is useful to review `H` and `(H)`.
- If the response includes clear human action, review `M`.
- Because form can be less stable here, review `FQ` carefully.
- If a popular response appears, it still has to be confirmed by formal criteria rather than familiarity alone.

## Cautions

- A figure that merely seems human does not automatically mean `H`; it may fit `(H)` better.
- The organizational difficulty of the card does not by itself make the response poor form.
- This page does not interpret the card; it only orients coding.

# [Coding/Cards] V

## Aliases

- Card V
- card V
- card 5
- plate V

## Definition

`Card V` often facilitates relatively clear form responses and global popular responses.  
This page summarizes coding points that are especially useful on that plate.

## Conditions

- `W` responses are common.
- The relatively clear form of the blot makes it useful to review `F` and `FQ`.

- `Card V` is not the same as determinant `V` for Vista.

# [Coding/Cards] VI

## Aliases

- Card VI
- card VI
- card 6
- plate VI

## Definition

`Card VI` often facilitates responses involving skin, texture, and form.  
This page summarizes what is useful to review in coding when those responses appear.

## Conditions

- Responses such as animal skin, leather, or hide rug are common.
- If the response uses touch or textural quality, review `T`, `TF`, or `FT` depending on the weight of form.
- If silhouette or form dominates without genuine tactile experience, review `F`.
- When the content is partial animal content, review `Ad`.
- If damage, stiffness, or deterioration is attributed to the skin or surface, also review `MOR`.

## Cautions

- Mentioning skin does not automatically imply a texture determinant.
- If tactile quality does not actually participate in the perception, do not add `T`.
- `Card VI` may facilitate certain popular responses, but `Popular` still has to be confirmed by formal criteria.

# [Coding/Cards] VII

## Aliases

- Card VII
- card VII
- card 7
- plate VII

## Definition

`Card VII` often facilitates heads, faces, and partial human figures.  
This page summarizes what to review in human content, organization, and movement.

## Conditions

- Face, head, or other partial human responses are common.
- If the response is partial, review `Hd` before `H`.
- If the scene shows clear human action, review `M`.
- When the organization among figures or zones becomes important, it may also be useful to review `Z`.
- Human content may also lead you to review `GHR / PHR`.

## Cautions

- A response that looks human does not automatically mean full human content `H`.
- Two profiles or two faces do not by themselves create a relational code.
- This page remains a coding note, not a symbolic interpretation of the card.

## Aliases

- Card VIII
- card VIII

## Definition

`Card VIII` often facilitates animal responses and can make the participation of color more noticeable.  
This page summarizes those coding focal points.

- Animal responses and popular responses tied to relatively clear zones are common.
- If color participates in building the response, review `FC`, `CF`, or `C`.

- Visible color on the card is not enough by itself for a chromatic determinant.
- Not every animal response on this card is `Popular`.

# [Coding/Cards] X

## Aliases

- Card X
- card X
- card 10
- plate X

## Definition

`Card X` combines many areas and many colors, so it often requires good delimitation of the response.  
This page summarizes the coding focal points that are most useful for that complexity.

## Conditions

- Review `Popular` when a clearly organized typical response appears.
- If color participates in the perception, review `FC`, `CF`, or `C`.
- If the response relies on multiple fragments and form becomes doubtful, review `FQ-`.
- The fact that the card is complex does not replace the need to describe the actual response clearly.

## Cautions

- A lot of color does not automatically mean a chromatic determinant.
- A lot of visual complexity does not automatically mean a Special Score.
- Coding still has to follow the actual response, not the apparent complexity of the plate.

en.title: [Coding/Content] Contents
en.bodyMarkdown:
# [Coding/Content] Contents

## Aliases

- Contents
- content codes
- human content
- animal content

## Definition

Content codes answer the question "what is it" that the person saw in the blot.  
They do not explain why it looked that way; that belongs to determinants.

## Conditions

- Content is assigned from the object or class of object named by the person.
- One response may receive more than one content code if the person truly describes more than one class of object.
- Each content code is recorded only once within a response.
- Human contents include [scoring-input/contents/H](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FH), [scoring-input/contents/(H)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28H%29), [scoring-input/contents/Hd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHd), [scoring-input/contents/(Hd)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Hd%29), and [scoring-input/contents/Hx](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHx).
- Animal and anatomy contents include [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA), [scoring-input/contents/(A)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28A%29), [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd), [scoring-input/contents/(Ad)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Ad%29), and [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn).
- Art, cultural-historical, blood, and botanical contents are coded as [scoring-input/contents/Art](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FArt), [scoring-input/contents/Ay](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAy), [scoring-input/contents/Bl](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FBl), and [scoring-input/contents/Bt](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FBt).
- Clothing, cloud, explosion, and fire or smoke contents are coded as [scoring-input/contents/Cg](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FCg), [scoring-input/contents/Cl](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FCl), [scoring-input/contents/Ex](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FEx), and [scoring-input/contents/Fi](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FFi).
- Food, geography, and household contents are coded as [scoring-input/contents/Fd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FFd), [scoring-input/contents/Ge](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FGe), and [scoring-input/contents/Hh](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHh).
- Landscape, nature, science, sexual, X-ray, and idiographic contents are coded as [scoring-input/contents/Ls](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FLs), [scoring-input/contents/Na](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FNa), [scoring-input/contents/Sc](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FSc), [scoring-input/contents/Sx](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FSx), [scoring-input/contents/Xy](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FXy), and [scoring-input/contents/Id](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FId).
- These content codes later combine with additional decisions such as `GHR/PHR`, `PureH`, or `H ratio`.

## Cautions

- Content and determinant are different axes. A response may have human content and, at the same time, form, movement, or color determinants.
- The human cluster has to separate whole realistic people, whole imaginary people, human details, imaginary human details, and human experience.
- The animal cluster has to separate whole realistic animals, whole imaginary animals, animal details, imaginary animal details, and anatomy-focused responses.
- The art/culture/basic nature cluster has to separate artistic objects, cultural-historical references, blood, and botanical material.
- The clothing/atmospheric/event cluster has to separate garments, clouds, explosions, and fire/smoke.
- The food/map/household cluster has to separate edible content, cartographic representation, and domestic objects.
- The landscape/nature/science/sexual/X-ray/idiographic cluster has to separate scenery, general nature, scientific objects, explicit sexual content, X-ray format, and true last-resort idiographic content.
- `Hx` does not code a whole person. It codes a clearly attributed human experience, feeling, or state.
- `An` is not just any animal part; it requires an anatomical or internal-structure focus.
- `Art` is not the same as `Ay`; one centers on artwork or decoration, and the other on cultural or historical reference.
- `Bl` codes blood as content, not color as a determinant.
- `Cl`, `Ex`, and `Fi` can look visually close, but they separate cloud, explosion, and fire/smoke content.
- `Fd` as content is not the same as [scoring-input/determinants/FD](ref://scoring-input%2Fdeterminants%2FFD) as a determinant.
- If `Na` applies with `Bt` or `Ls`, record `Na` only. If `Na` is absent but both `Bt` and `Ls` apply, record only the one that best represents the response.
- `Xy` is not simply another way to write `An`; when `Xy` is recorded, do not add `An` to the same response.
- `Id` is a last resort and should not absorb responses that fit better under `Sc` or `Art`.
- Human content by itself does not decide [scoring-input/gphr/GHR](ref://scoring-input%2Fgphr%2FGHR) or [scoring-input/gphr/PHR](ref://scoring-input%2Fgphr%2FPHR); those require an additional coding step.

# [Coding/Content] (A)

## Aliases

- (A)
- imaginary animal
- fictional whole animal

## Definition

`(A)` is coded when the content is a whole animal, but fantastic, mythic, or clearly invented.  
The form is still a whole animal, even though the referent does not exist in ordinary reality.

## Conditions

- The response must describe a whole animal rather than only a part.
- The fantastic quality may come from mythology, fairy tales, cartoons, or the person's own invention.
- Typical examples are a dragon, unicorn, or monster with a whole animal form.
- If the referent is a realistic whole animal, first consider [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA).
- If only part of a fantastic animal is described, first consider [scoring-input/contents/(Ad)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Ad%29).

## Cautions

- `(A)` and [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA) are separated by reality versus fantasy, not by how complete the figure is.
- `(A)` and [scoring-input/contents/(Ad)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Ad%29) are separated by whole versus partial animal form.
- Content does not replace the later decision about determinant, `FQ`, or `Popular`.

## Cross References

# [Coding/Content] (Ad)

## Aliases

- (Ad)
- imaginary animal detail
- fictional animal detail

## Definition

`(Ad)` is coded when the person describes a part of a fantastic, mythic, or invented animal.  
It is the partial and imaginary member of the animal cluster.

## Conditions

- The response has to point to an animal part rather than a whole animal.
- The referent must be fantastic, fictional, or clearly invented.
- Typical examples are a dragon wing, monster claw, or horn from a mythic creature.
- If the fantastic animal appears as a whole figure, first consider [scoring-input/contents/(A)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28A%29).
- If the detail belongs to a realistic animal, first consider [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd).

## Cautions

- `(Ad)` and [scoring-input/contents/(A)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28A%29) are separated by part versus whole.
- `(Ad)` and [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd) are separated by fantasy versus reality.
- Even though it is imaginary, the content is still an animal detail rather than a human part; compare with [scoring-input/contents/Hd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHd) when needed.

# [Coding/Content] (H)

## Aliases

- (H)
- imaginary human
- mythic human figure

## Definition

`(H)` is coded when the percept is a whole human figure from fiction, fantasy, or mythology.  
It is still a whole human figure, but not an ordinary realistic person.

## Conditions

- The main object has to be a whole human figure.
- The figure must be fantastic, mythic, fictional, or clearly unrealistic.
- Typical examples include angels, demons, giants, fairies, ghosts, or science-fiction humanoids.
- If only a part of that figure is described, reconsider [scoring-input/contents/(Hd)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Hd%29).

## Cautions

- `(H)` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/H](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FH); `H` is reserved for realistic whole human figures.
- `(H)` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/(Hd)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Hd%29); `(Hd)` is used for an imaginary human detail.
- A costume, mask, or artistic style does not automatically change the code if the person is still describing a realistic whole person.

# [Coding/Content] (Hd)

## Aliases

- (Hd)
- imaginary human detail
- mythic human detail

## Definition

`(Hd)` is coded when the response describes only a part of a fantastic, mythic, or fictional human figure.  
It is the imaginary counterpart of `Hd`.

## Conditions

- The main content has to be an incomplete human detail.
- That detail has to belong to a nonrealistic, fantastic, or mythic figure.
- Typical examples include a demon's head, a witch's arm, an angel's eyes, or humanoid parts of a fantasy creature.
- If the response describes a whole fantastic figure, go back to [scoring-input/contents/(H)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28H%29).

## Cautions

- `(Hd)` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/Hd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHd); the key difference is the imaginary or mythic character.
- `(Hd)` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/(H)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28H%29); `(H)` requires a whole figure.
- Many `(Hd)` responses also call for review of [scoring-input/gphr/PHR](ref://scoring-input%2Fgphr%2FPHR), but that decision is still separate.
- Do not use `(Hd)` just because the response seems odd; the person must actually describe an unrealistic human part.

# [Coding/Content] A

## Aliases

- A
- whole animal
- real animal

## Definition

`A` is coded when the response content is a whole, realistic animal.  
It does not refer to an animal part or a fantastic creature.

## Conditions

- The seen figure must organize as a whole animal.
- The referent has to be recognizable as a real animal, not an imagined one.
- Typical examples are a whole dog, bat, butterfly, or bird.
- If only part of the animal appears, first consider [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd).
- If the whole animal is fantastic, mythic, or invented, first consider [scoring-input/contents/(A)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28A%29).

## Cautions

- `A` and [scoring-input/contents/(A)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28A%29) share the idea of a whole animal, but differ in whether the referent is real or imagined.
- `A` and [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd) are separated by wholeness, not by size.
- `A` content by itself does not decide `Popular`, `FQ`, or the determinant.

# [Coding/Content] Ad

## Aliases

- Ad
- animal detail
- partial animal

## Definition

`Ad` is coded when the response names a part or detail of an animal rather than the whole animal.  
It covers a tail, head, wing, claw, or other clearly partial animal feature.

## Conditions

- The focus of the response must be on a part of the animal, not on the whole figure.
- The detail may be external, such as a paw or head, as long as it stays a partial animal feature.
- If the figure is a whole realistic animal, first consider [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA).
- If the detail belongs to a fantastic or imaginary animal, first consider [scoring-input/contents/(Ad)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Ad%29).
- If the emphasis is on anatomy or internal structure, first consider [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn).

## Cautions

- `Ad` and [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA) are separated by part versus whole.
- `Ad` and [scoring-input/contents/(Ad)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28Ad%29) are separated by reality versus fantasy.
- `Ad` and [scoring-input/contents/Hd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHd) are both detail codes, but one is animal and the other is human.
- Not every biological fragment is `Ad`; if the idea is strongly anatomical, [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn) may be the better fit.

# [Coding/Content] An

## Aliases

- An
- anatomy
- anatomical content

## Definition

`An` is coded when the response centers on anatomy, body structure, or internal parts.  
It is not enough that the response seems like an animal fragment; the main idea has to be anatomical.

## Conditions

- Use it for bones, organs, musculature, or internal bodily structure.
- The main criterion is that the response points to anatomy rather than only to an external animal part.
- If the figure is only an external animal part, first consider [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd).
- If the response turns into a diagrammatic or illustrative anatomy image, [scoring-input/contents/Art](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FArt) may also be added when appropriate.
- If the response is seen as an X-ray or radiograph, record [scoring-input/contents/Xy](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FXy) instead of `An`.

## Cautions

- `An` and [scoring-input/contents/Ad](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAd) can look close, but `An` requires an anatomical focus.
- `An` is not assigned just because the person mentions a body part; the response should sound internal, structural, or biological.
- When `Xy` is recorded, do not add `An` to the same response.
- This content often matters later for routes such as [scoring-input/gphr/PHR](ref://scoring-input%2Fgphr%2FPHR) or [result-interpretation/lower-section/selfPerception/An_Xy](ref://result-interpretation%2Flower-section%2FselfPerception%2FAn_Xy), but it does not determine them by itself.

# [Coding/Content] Art

## Aliases

- Art
- art
- art object
- decorative object

## Definition

`Art` is coded when the main content is perceived as an artistic work, decorative object, or aesthetic product.  
The key point is not just seeing an object, but understanding it as something artistic or ornamental.

## Conditions

- Use it for paintings, statues, drawings, sculptures, emblems, or decorative pieces.
- It may be added together with another content code if the response names both the object and its artistic character.
- If the response is mainly anatomy or biological structure, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn).
- If the main emphasis is historical, ethnic, or anthropological meaning rather than art object status, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Ay](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAy).

## Cautions

- `Art` and [scoring-input/contents/Ay](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAy) can co-occur, but they do not mean the same thing.
- `Art` centers on artwork or decoration; `Ay` centers on cultural or historical reference.
- A biological image presented like a mounted specimen or stylized illustration may take [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn) as the main content and `Art` as a secondary code.

# [Coding/Content] Ay

## Aliases

- Ay
- anthropology
- cultural content
- historical content

## Definition

`Ay` is coded when the response includes a specific historical, ethnic, cultural, or anthropological reference.  
It is not enough to see a person or object; the response has to carry a recognizable cultural frame.

## Conditions

- Use it for figures, clothing, weapons, symbols, or scenes tied to a culture, era, or civilization.
- It may be combined with [scoring-input/contents/H](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FH), [scoring-input/contents/(H)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28H%29), or [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA) when the main object is still a person or animal.
- The key criterion is historical or cultural marking, not mere appearance.
- If the response sounds more like an artwork or decorative piece than a cultural reference, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Art](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FArt).

## Cautions

- `Ay` and [scoring-input/contents/Art](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FArt) may look close, but `Ay` depends on cultural or historical context.
- Do not code `Ay` only because a response sounds exotic; the cultural reference has to be identifiable.
- `Ay` often works as an additional content code rather than the only descriptive axis.

# [Coding/Content] Bl

## Aliases

- Bl
- blood
- bleeding

## Definition

`Bl` is coded when the main content is blood.  
It does not refer to a full anatomical structure; it refers to blood itself or the idea of bleeding.

## Conditions

- Use it when the person names blood, a stream of blood, a blood stain, or bleeding.
- It may be coded whether the blood is understood as human or animal.
- If the response mainly centers on bones, organs, or body structure, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn).
- If the blood is part of a human or animal figure, `Bl` may be combined with [scoring-input/contents/H](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FH) or [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA) when appropriate.

## Cautions

- `Bl` is not a color code; it does not replace chromatic determinant coding.
- `Bl` and [scoring-input/contents/An](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAn) may both sound biological, but `Bl` centers on blood and `An` on anatomy.
- It is not enough that the blot looks red. The person has to name blood or a clearly equivalent idea.

- If `Na` applies with `Bt`, record `Na` only and do not add `Bt`.
- If `Na` is absent but both `Bt` and `Ls` apply, record only the one that best represents the response.
- If the response describes an animal or animal detail, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA) or its variants.
- If the focus shifts to blood or biological injury, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Bl](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FBl).

## Cautions

- `Bt` is botanical content, not a judgment about color, texture, or shape.
- Do not use it just because something looks organic; the response has to organize it specifically as plant material.
- `Bt`, `Ls`, and `Na` all contribute to the Isolation Index, so they are not counted together within one response.
- Some sources write `BT`; this application uses the Comprehensive System code `Bt`.

# [Coding/Content] Cg

## Aliases

- Cg
- clothing
- garment
- wearable

## Definition

`Cg` is coded when the main content is clothing, a garment, or a wearable accessory.  
The decisive point is that the form is understood as something worn on the body.

## Conditions

- Use it for hat, boot, glove, cape, dress, uniform, or another recognizable item of clothing.
- It may also be used for body-worn accessories when the response treats them as part of dress.

- If the emphasis falls on decorative or artistic value, it may also require [scoring-input/contents/Art](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FArt).

- `Cg` is not used for just any object. The response has to identify clothing or a wearable accessory.
- `Cg` and [scoring-input/contents/Ay](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAy) may coexist, but `Ay` needs cultural or historical framing.

# [Coding/Content] Cl

## Aliases

- Cl
- cloud
- clouds

## Definition

`Cl` is coded when the main content is a cloud.  
It is used for the cloud itself, not for every similar atmospheric form.

## Conditions

- Use it when the person names a cloud, cloud layer, or form clearly organized as a cloud.
- The cloud has to be the main content and not just a vague background.
- If the image is better understood as mist, vapor, or haze, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Na](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FNa).
- If the form is seen as smoke or fire, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Fi](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FFi).

- `Cl` and [scoring-input/contents/Na](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FNa) split cloud from mist or vapor.
- `Cl` and [scoring-input/contents/Fi](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FFi) can look visually close, but `Fi` requires smoke or fire content.
- It is not enough that something looks diffuse. The person has to organize it as a cloud.

# [Coding/Content] Ex

## Aliases

- Ex
- explosion
- blast

## Definition

`Ex` is coded when the main content is an explosion or an explosive scene.  
The key point is the bursting event itself, not just smoke or brightness.

## Conditions

- Use it for explosion, blast, detonation, or a clearly named explosive scene.
- It may include sparks or debris as long as the person keeps the central idea of explosion.
- If the main focus is fire or smoke rather than explosion, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Fi](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FFi).

## Cautions

- `Ex` and [scoring-input/contents/Fi](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FFi) may coexist visually, but they are not the same code.
- `Ex` requires an explosive event; `Fi` requires fire or smoke as the main content.
- Do not use `Ex` for a mere sense of energy or motion.

## Cross References

- [[Coding/Content] Contents](ref://scoring-input/contents)
- [[Coding/Content] Fi](ref://scoring-input/contents/Fi)

# [Coding/Content] Fd

## Aliases

- Fd
- food
- edible object

## Definition

`Fd` is coded when the main content is food or something understood as edible.  
It is a content code, not a determinant.

## Conditions

- Use it for prepared food, a meal, meat, cake, served fruit, or another clearly edible item.
- It may also be used when the scene is organized around eating or a clearly edible object.
- If the main focus is the animal itself rather than food, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/A](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FA) or another animal content code.
- Do not confuse it with [scoring-input/determinants/FD](ref://scoring-input%2Fdeterminants%2FFD), which belongs to determinants.

## Cautions

- `Fd` as content and [scoring-input/determinants/FD](ref://scoring-input%2Fdeterminants%2FFD) as determinant belong to different coding axes.
- `Fd` and botanical content can seem close when vegetables are named, but `Fd` requires that they be organized as food.
- The later interpersonal meaning of [result-interpretation/lower-section/interpersonal/Food](ref://result-interpretation%2Flower-section%2Finterpersonal%2FFood) does not change the coding decision itself.

# [Coding/Content] Fi

## Aliases

- Fi
- fire
- smoke

## Definition

`Fi` is coded when the main content is fire or smoke.  
The response has to organize the blot as flame, fire, smoke, or a column of smoke.

## Conditions

- Use it for flames, fire, burning, smoke, or a smoke column when they are clearly named.
- The focus should stay on fire or smoke themselves.
- If the response emphasizes explosion or detonation, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Ex](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FEx).
- If the person is describing clouds, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Cl](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FCl).

## Cautions

- `Fi` and [scoring-input/contents/Ex](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FEx) are not separated by visual intensity; they are separated by the named content.
- `Fi` and [scoring-input/contents/Cl](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FCl) can look alike when the form is diffuse, but one is smoke/fire and the other is cloud.
- Do not assign `Fi` just because of red or dark color; the person has to say fire or smoke.

# [Coding/Content] Ge

## Aliases

- Ge
- geography
- map
- cartographic content

## Definition

`Ge` is coded when the person organizes the response as a map, geographic plan, or cartographic representation.  
It does not refer to a real landscape scene; it refers to something read as a map.

## Conditions

- Use it for a map, atlas, geographic plan, or cartographic drawing of an area.
- It can apply to either a general map or a map of a specific region.
- The core criterion is cartographic representation, not natural scenery.
- If the person describes an actual landscape, mountains, or coastline as a scene, first reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Ls](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FLs).

## Cautions

- `Ge` and [scoring-input/contents/Ls](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FLs) split map from landscape.
- It is not enough that the form looks irregular or territorial. The person has to read it as a map or geographic plan.
- `Ge` is not used for abstract decoration without spatial reference.

## Cross References

- [[Coding/Content] Contents](ref://scoring-input/contents)
- [[Coding/Content] Ls](ref://scoring-input/contents/Ls)

# [Coding/Content] H

## Aliases

- H
- human
- whole human figure

## Definition

`H` is coded when the percept is a whole, realistic human figure.  
The response points to an entire person, not a body part and not a mythic or fantastic figure.

## Conditions

- The main object has to be a whole human figure.
- The figure must be presented as realistically human, not fantasy or mythology.
- If the figure is historically or culturally specific, [scoring-input/contents/Ay](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FAy) may be added as a secondary content code.
- If only a body part is described, reconsider [scoring-input/contents/Hd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHd).

## Cautions

- `H` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/(H)](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2F%28H%29); `(H)` is reserved for fictional or mythic whole human figures.
- `H` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/Hd](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHd); `Hd` is used for an incomplete human detail.
- `H` is not the same as [scoring-input/contents/Hx](ref://scoring-input%2Fcontents%2FHx); `Hx` codes human experience rather than a person.
- Human content alone does not settle [scoring-input/gphr/GHR](ref://scoring-input%2Fgphr%2FGHR) or [scoring-input/gphr/PHR](ref://scoring-input%2Fgphr%2FPHR).
